cards.name: assemble-then-type-flyin
cards.summary: Textless component shells fly in from every direction onto an empty dark grid, then every character arrives from 3D space with its own large rotation and settles into position.
cards.use: Openings where a page or poster "grows itself"; capability showcases for typography and layout products; two-stage narrative from wireframe to finished design
cards.energy: Medium-high (sparse during wireframe phase, dense during text phase, monotonically rising toward the finale)
cards.intention: Split "page generation" into two semantically distinct stages: first assemble the wireframe skeleton (frames, cards, dividers, color blocks, all textless), then populate the text. Text characters arrive with individual 3D rotational landings because the skeleton stage uses only 2D planar translation—the two stages must inhabit different motion dimensions, otherwise viewers cannot register that "this is step two."

styles.label: Assemble Then Type Flyin
styles.description: Textless component shells fly in from every direction onto an empty dark grid, then every character arrives from 3D space with its own large rotation and settles into position.

cards.name: aurora-bloom-bg-flip
cards.summary: A soft purple-orange aurora blob rises from the bottom of a light frame, then the whole background slams dark in under half a second while the copy blur-swaps to a new line.
cards.use: Narrative turning points ("For many years... -> everything changed"); the pivotal beat shifting from prelude to main emphasis in brand films; chapter transitions between light and dark palettes
cards.energy: Low to high (first 2/3 builds anticipation; the darkening snap delivers the primary accent)
cards.intention: Treat "background inversion" as an accent mark: let the aurora slowly rise over the first 56% so viewers adapt to the light canvas, then snap the entire screen to near-black in under 0.4s—this impact reads more decisively as "turning the page" than any zoom or white flash. The copy swap must lock immediately after the inversion, leaving a distinct gap between lines so viewers absorb the visual change before reading the new message.

styles.label: Aurora Bloom Bg Flip
styles.description: A soft purple-orange aurora blob rises from the bottom of a light frame, then the whole background slams dark in under half a second while the copy blur-swaps to a new line.

cards.name: autolayout-gap-dial
cards.summary: A gap value dial pushes a row of blocks apart in real time while badge digits tick, then everything springs back into place.
cards.use: Feature showcase shots for design tools/low-code products highlighting "change a number, UI reacts in real time"; category language packaging using design tool semantics
cards.duration: ~5s (150f: marquee box-select entrance + prep pull-back 10f + expansion 34f + breath hold 20f + spring rebound + settle hold)
cards.energy: Medium (tool rationality style; satisfaction lies in locked synchronization between numbers and displacement)
cards.intention: "Parameters change, UI responds" is the core promise of design tools, but it is typically filmed as a before-and-after cut: "click panel -> switch result," discarding causality. This shot captures causality as a continuous take: the gap badge digits tick step-by-step, the linked blocks are pushed apart in the **same frame**, and measurement lines stretch in real time—the numbers are the reins, the layout is the horse. The marquee outline + 8 handles + gap annotations speak the native language of design tools, allowing viewers to immediately recognize "adjusting parameters inside a tool." The return journey deliberately uses an underdamped spring overshoot (compressing tighter than the starting point before restabilizing), turning "return to position" into an elastic resolution. Division of labor with type-and-filter: that card handles retrieval causality ("input content -> list converges"), while this card handles parameter causality ("dial value -> geometric rearrangement").

styles.label: Autolayout Gap Dial
styles.description: A gap value dial pushes a row of blocks apart in real time while badge digits tick, then everything springs back into place.

cards.name: avatar-bracket-carousel
cards.summary: A four-corner focus bracket stays locked mid-sentence while a vertical queue of avatars springs through it three times, each one sharpening and growing as it enters the frame and shrinking, dimming and blurring as it leaves.
cards.use: Capability enumeration for "one slot, multiple roles"; core one-sentence shot for team, identity, preset, or persona products.
cards.energy: Medium (Three equidistant switches form a steady metronome; focus bracket pulse is the only decorative motion)
cards.intention: Listing "our agent can act as director, editor, animator, sound designer" as four lines is just a checklist. Packing it into a single slot in a sentence turns it into a promise plus four proofs: the sentence stays still while only the person in the slot changes. The four-corner focus bracket is key to this technique—it does not rotate, but it pins the viewer's eyes onto that 92×92 box, so the four replacements read as "the exact same slot" rather than "four avatars floating by."

styles.label: Avatar Bracket Carousel
styles.description: A four-corner focus bracket stays locked mid-sentence while a vertical queue of avatars springs through it three times, each one sharpening and growing as it enters the frame and shrinking, dimming and blurring as it leaves.

cards.name: basic-3d-scene
cards.summary: Impress-style spatial slides: cards sit at scattered 3D poses and the camera flies to align with each one by inverting its transform, ending on a pulled-back overview where every card lights up.
cards.use: Spatial storytelling for concepts, roadmaps, or a 3-step framework; replaces flat 2D slides with a "different spatial perspective for every step"
cards.duration: ~7.5s (225f@30fps; four stops, three flight segments 28/32/32f, hold >=30f per stop)
cards.energy: Medium (spatial surprise on each transition, quiet card reading during hold)
cards.intention: Turn "page flipping" into "traveling through an idea space": each card has not only a position but also a 3D pose (the second stop tilts the world left by 38°, the third stop lays the frame on its side by 90°), and as the camera aligns to each card, the viewer's world rotates with it—the spatial transformation itself creates a sense of ceremony for entering each new chapter.

styles.label: Basic 3D Scene
styles.description: Impress-style spatial slides: cards sit at scattered 3D poses and the camera flies to align with each one by inverting its transform, ending on a pulled-back overview where every card lights up.

cards.name: beat-cut-moves
cards.summary: A three-flash freeze montage: white flashes hard-cut through different crops of the same subject and settle on the key number.
cards.use: Highlight sequences turning the "cut" itself into a drumbeat; award-style paparazzi ceremony, crowning key metrics
cards.energy: High
cards.intention: The library's rhythm vocabulary historically governed velocities "within a single continuous movement" (speed-ramp-freeze pauses and unfreezes a single take) and "hold durations after settling" (R-series breathing precedents), with no terms governing **how cut points are arranged across multiple shots**. This card fills that void: hard cuts employ zero transition easing, turning the cut intervals themselves into musical notation—three white flashes with tightening intervals (22f -> 18f), reading as a paparazzi shutter burst (Variant A). It does not conflict with R-series precedents: R governs pauses after settling, whereas this card governs cut arrangement; the cutting flurry must conclude with an ample resting hold to restore breathing space. Note that this is a deliberate exception: the pace preference precedent mandates "slowing down," so the harder the cutting flurry strikes, the longer the concluding hold must be.

styles.label: Paparazzi Flash
styles.description: Three white flashes each hard-cut to a different crop of the same subject (wide, card, digits), settling on the number.
styles.use: Highlight moment ceremony: award bursts, key number coronation

cards.name: beat-step-list-theme-cycle
cards.summary: An adjective list steps up one row per beat while a fixed center pill catches each word and the background recolors on the same beat.
cards.use: "One product, many personalities / themes" showcases (adjective runs like modern / playful / expressive); the highest rhythmic density section in the film; syncing to musical beats
cards.duration: Setup 30f + 18f per beat x beat count + ending hold; 4 beats ≈ 4.7s (demo 140f)
cards.energy: High (three channels jumping in unison every 0.6s delivers high density energy)
cards.intention: Switching a theme color once is a feature demo; switching every 0.6 seconds three times in a row—with "selected row + pill color + canvas background" jumping in unison on the exact same frame—creates a metronome. It produces the highest rhythmic density in the entire video using the most economical variable switches. Two requirements are non-negotiable: first, **all three channels must lock to the exact same beat**—if any channel lags by even half a beat, the synchronized jump degenerates into three disjointed animations; second, **the boundary between jumping and sliding**—the jump window occupies only the first 6f of the beat, with the remaining 12f resting completely static. Beats must "jump," not "slide"; a smoothly scrolling list is merely a list.

styles.label: Beat Step List Theme Cycle
styles.description: An adjective list steps up one row per beat while a fixed center pill catches each word and the background recolors on the same beat.

cards.name: before-after-slider-scrub
cards.summary: Before and after views share one frame while a fast-then-slow slider reveals the processed result.
cards.use: Feature comparison segments for AI enhancement, optimization, or refactoring ("before vs after" explained in a single shot)
cards.energy: Medium (fast scrub is the impact beat, slow sweep is the reading window)
cards.intention: The standard comparison syntax for AI visual product promo videos: the "before" view (low contrast, hazy) and "after" view (crisp, processed) share one frame; a vertical divider bar with a circular handle first whips rapidly from the left edge to 70% (with overshoot rebound), pauses for a beat, then slowly sweeps back at roughly 1/5 speed to let the audience inspect the differences—**the speed contrast between fast whip and slow sweep creates the rhythm**: the fast whip announces "it changed," and the slow sweep proves "how it changed."

styles.label: Before After Slider Scrub
styles.description: Before and after views share one frame while a fast-then-slow slider reveals the processed result.

cards.name: bezier-source-converge-merge
cards.summary: Four source nodes each draw a thin bezier curve toward one convergence point, then slide along their own curve and shrink as if swallowed, while accent data packets glide the paths and the curves erase backward.
cards.use: Core mechanism shot for "multi-source integration / unified access / data convergence"; explanatory section for integration, aggregation, and single-entry products.
cards.energy: Medium (Slow long-take push, maintaining vitality via gliding packets; swallow moment is the only subtle peak)
cards.intention: "We unified four sources" is an abstract claim. This motion turns it into a visible physical process: first establish four independent channels (draw-on means "connected"), then have the four sources slide along their respective curves into the exact same point and get swallowed (shrinking to 0 means "absorbed"), and finally erase the paths leaving only the brand logo ("now there is only one"). Each of the three narrative stages has clear start and end points, letting viewers grasp the cause and effect without voiceover.

styles.label: Bezier Source Converge Merge
styles.description: Four source nodes each draw a thin bezier curve toward one convergence point, then slide along their own curve and shrink as if swallowed, while accent data packets glide the paths and the curves erase backward.

cards.name: blur-slide
cards.summary: Title words rise into place one after another as vertical offset, blur, and opacity converge on a single shared ease, with the subtitle following before the title settles.
cards.use: Ideal for almost all paired title/subtitle scenarios; hero section copy on product pages, chapter subtitles; the default text reveal when seeking a "professional yet understated" feel
cards.energy: Low (single-shot convergence, no peak, no loop)
cards.intention: This is the **default solution** for text reveals — no spectacle, no mechanical gimmick, just placing words gently into position one by one. Its sense of professionalism comes entirely from one thing: the three channels of y, blur, and opacity share the same progress `p` and the same easing curve, so words "emerge from defocus" rather than "slide in and happen to fade in." When a video already has heavy techniques elsewhere (glitch, reels), the title should use this card to yield the spotlight to the hero.

styles.label: Blur Slide
styles.description: Title words rise into place one after another as vertical offset, blur, and opacity converge on a single shared ease, with the subtitle following before the title settles.

cards.name: bottom-push-stack-wipe
cards.summary: Each new scene pushes up from the bottom edge with its own saturated background color, physically shoving the old scene out of frame.
cards.use: Section-change backbone for multi-chapter product promos (each chapter features one selling point with one distinct background color); paragraph transitions requiring a "page-turn rhythm" running throughout the entire video.
cards.duration: Demo three consecutive pushes 170f (~5.7s); single push 26f + in-chapter hold ~1.2s.
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intention: In wipe-transitions, a boundary sweeps across while both the old and new pages remain stationary; in page-turn, the old page splits open like double doors and slides out. This card introduces a third physical dynamic: **the new chapter shoves the old chapter out**—the two screens maintain rigid contact, moving at identical speed in the same direction, like vending machine push-stacking. The crux is "moving the entire screen along with its background color": the background color + window card + decorative strips are fused into a single slab that pushes in from the bottom edge, communicating to the audience that "the world has changed" rather than just "a card was swapped." A heavy ease-out (fast enter, slow settle) gives the push an authoritative "thunk" landing; the 40px seam shadow along the top edge serves as physical evidence of contact between the two screens. Chaining three consecutive pushes with fully saturated background colors turns the chapter transitions themselves into the metronome of the entire video—the original Slack promo relied entirely on this single technique as its structural backbone.

styles.label: Bottom Push Stack Wipe
styles.description: Each new scene pushes up from the bottom edge with its own saturated background color, physically shoving the old scene out of frame.

cards.name: brace-expand
cards.summary: A tight pair of braces appears at center, then springs apart and scales up to title size, revealing the text through a clip width bound strictly to the brace gap.
cards.use: Title cards for developer/technical products; chapter openers; minimalist single beats where "a single symbol completes the reveal"
cards.duration: ~4s (120f@30fps: cursor 0–6f → 6f small braces hard-cut → 14f spring open → 40–64f kerning relaxation → subtitle → hold)
cards.energy: Medium (single overshoot is the only peak, remaining stationary)
cards.intention: Among all title reveal techniques, this card is the most economical: no mask bars, no character-by-character reveals, no displacement — just a pair of braces expanding sideways while the text is "bracketed out." It naturally carries the semantics of code (`{}` are curly braces), so in the context of technical products it reads as "this is the content itself." The critical point is that clip width **must be strictly bound to brace positions**: once text fades in or wipes in on its own, the braces degrade into mere decoration, completely destroying the curtain effect.

styles.label: Brace Expand
styles.description: A tight pair of braces appears at center, then springs apart and scales up to title size, revealing the text through a clip width bound strictly to the brace gap.

cards.name: brand-frame-snap
cards.summary: A thick brand-color frame grows around the screen before content arrives, then hard-flips its color on the same frame the inner layout switches.
cards.use: Global packaging layer for dual-mode or dual-chapter product videos (blue = Mode A, green = Mode B color coding); branded wrapping for live screen recordings
cards.duration: Single color flip ~4.7s (140f); the frame itself can persist across the full video
cards.energy: Medium (high at the flip moment, quiet packaging layer otherwise)
cards.intention: Raw screen recordings filling the entire canvas lack brand presence, while logo watermarks feel cheap. This card frames screen recordings with a thick brand-color border: the frame **appears before content** (establishing the frame before hanging the picture creates ceremony), after which the frame color becomes the semantic code for the entire video—in the demo, cobalt blue = Design, orange-red = Dev Mode (original reference was blue/green; the key is complementary hue clash + lightness contrast). During chapter switches, the full frame snaps color within a single frame with zero gradient; this hard cut visually equals a mechanical gear-shift sound effect. Simultaneously, the inner window layout switches A->B and corner badges/wordmarks update synchronously, locking in the "mode switch" through 3-point harmonic resonance. Division of labor with theme-switch-moves: that card alters the UI body theme (with sweeping wipe boundaries), whereas this card switches the outer "framing layer" (single-frame boundaryless cut) to signal mode/chapter switches rather than UI skinning.

styles.label: Brand Frame Snap
styles.description: A thick brand-color frame grows around the screen before content arrives, then hard-flips its color on the same frame the inner layout switches.

cards.name: brand-ink-open
cards.summary: Ink crosshairs draw in, the wordmark stamps letter by letter, a subtitle types on, then the lockup holds and lifts away.
cards.use: Brand opening; any title sequence that establishes the brand identity before entering the product
cards.energy: Low (starting position, leaves climbing room for subsequent shots)
cards.intention: Establishing brand memory on the very first beat: before any product visual appears, viewers clearly recognize and remember the name. Quiet, paper-and-ink texture, with a complete moment of stillness.

styles.label: Brand Ink Open
styles.description: Ink crosshairs draw in, the wordmark stamps letter by letter, a subtitle types on, then the lockup holds and lifts away.

cards.name: canvas-materialize-moves
cards.summary: Two materialize moves: table rows arc out of a panel and morph into canvas cards, and a typed prompt grows a cascading diagram tree.
cards.use: Narrative sequences in AI/collaboration tools where "generated results land on a canvas"; Style A demonstrates "existing content transitioning into a new form of existence," while Style B demonstrates "a structured tree growing from a single sentence"
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intention: Existing generation narratives in the library only cover "typing inside a window" (document-typewriter-reveal, where documents write themselves) and "charts coming alive" (chart-live-moves), with no vocabulary for **content leaving its container and materializing as new entities on an open canvas**. This card fills that gap: the canvas is the stage, and generated objects are actors entering the scene. The linchpin of Style A is cross-container morphological transition—identical content shifts from "row" to "card," with position, width, height, corner radius, and layout interpolating synchronously along a single spring, so viewers register "it flew over and transformed" rather than "one deleted, another added." The linchpin of Style B is cascading hierarchy: lines lead nodes, and levels feed subsequent levels; structural clarity stems from sequential progression rather than simultaneous appearance.

styles.label: Panel To Canvas
styles.description: Checkboxes tick themselves, then table rows arc out of the panel and morph mid-flight into canvas cards, landing with casual tilts.
styles.use: Batch import / one-click to canvas: content migrates from list state to spatial layout

styles.label: Diagram Cascade
styles.description: A typed prompt sprouts a diagram tree: root, children, grandchildren pop layer by layer with connector lines drawing ahead of each node.
styles.use: AI-generated diagrams / mindmaps / ER trees: a typed prompt sprouts a tree

cards.name: card-flip-reveal
cards.summary: Feature cards rotate 180 degrees around the Y axis, flash at the edge, and reveal a large result on the back.
cards.use: Paired "feature → outcome" narratives: a row of feature cards flipping one by one to reveal their respective metrics/conclusions; element-level transition card.
cards.duration: Total 150f (~5s, including hold); per card: 4f prep + 16f flip + ~10f spring settle; 12f stagger across three cards.
cards.energy: Medium-high
cards.intention: The library's "flip" family already includes the wipe-transitions blinds-slice (vanes flipping sequentially to execute a page turn). This card represents a **semantic flip**: the front and back of a card form a cause-and-effect pair—the front displays the feature UI, while the back reveals the quantitative conclusion it produces. The flip gesture itself serves as the answer to "So what?", a staple visual grammar of Apple bento segments. Staggered by 10f–12f across a row, three cards unveiling three figures deliver the distinct rhythm of a "rapid-fire impact report."

styles.label: Card Flip Reveal
styles.description: Feature cards rotate 180 degrees around the Y axis, flash at the edge, and reveal a large result on the back.

cards.name: card-flock-tumble
cards.summary: Three UI cards tumble in 3D from edge-on to a stepped formation, keep slowly rotating, then collapse inward and burst into a smoke ring under a giant word.
cards.use: Climax energy segments (explosive transition from feature UI cluster to brand slogan); neon/aurora dark-stage aesthetics; segments summarizing "multi-page capabilities" into a singular thesis.
cards.duration: Tumble ~1.5s + slow rotation showcase ~0.3s + inward collapse 0.3s + smoke ring + giant word ~2s; entire sequence 4.5s.
cards.energy: Extremely high (reserved for full-video energy peaks)
cards.intention: Three UI cards tumble and align in 3D space like dealt playing cards, holding a brief hero pose before instantly collapsing into the center, bursting into an expanding smoke ring as a massive brand title punches through the ring—"capability showcase → energy collapse → slogan explosion" in one continuous, breathless breath. Three non-negotiables define execution: **silkiness** (edge-on → tumble → stepped formation driven by a single continuous Catmull-Rom spline, as piecewise linear interpolation produces jarring velocity steps), **no stopping** (maintaining low-angular-velocity slow rotation upon landing until inward collapse; static holds were explicitly rejected in review: "do not stop, keep rotating"—climax sequences allow no frozen frames), and **tack-sharp clarity throughout** (motion blur and depth-of-field blur completely removed; rejected in review: "do not add blur effects").

styles.label: Card Flock Tumble
styles.description: Three UI cards tumble in 3D from edge-on to a stepped formation, keep slowly rotating, then collapse inward and burst into a smoke ring under a giant word.

cards.name: card-stack
cards.summary: Eight cards spring up from below the frame one after another and pile into a single stack, then the whole pile fans out into a 3D arc as each card rotates, slides sideways and steps back in depth.
cards.use: Product sections establishing "we offer a complete collection"; establishing shot for card walls, template libraries, or solution lists; also serves as anticipation beat before a logo reveal.
cards.energy: Medium-High (Entrance is a sequence of punchy pops; fanning phase consolidates into a single smooth group motion)
cards.intention: A deck of cards gathers into a single stack before fanning out into an ensemble—the sequence is vital: present the "whole" first, then reveal the "individual." The viewer first absorbs a substantial deck (conveying volume), and only on second glance notices each card is distinct (conveying diversity). Reserving the fanning move for the end ensures it does not compete with the entrance cadence.

styles.label: Card Stack
styles.description: Eight cards spring up from below the frame one after another and pile into a single stack, then the whole pile fans out into a 3D arc as each card rotates, slides sideways and steps back in depth.

cards.name: carousel-3d
cards.summary: Eight cards sit on a circular ring laid out with sin and cos, spinning through exactly one full revolution while each card billboards outward with matched front and back faces so it never reads as mirrored or upside down.
cards.use: Looping showcase for portfolios, template libraries, or integration directories; background plates or landing page heroes requiring seamless looping.
cards.energy: Medium (Steady-state infinitely loopable motion, with stops every 45° establishing cadence)
cards.intention: The simplest way to showcase "a set of items" is a horizontal slider, but sliders have a distinct beginning and end. A ring has neither—it loops naturally, so viewers never feel it has "finished playing" regardless of how long they watch. The core issue this card solves is the most common failure point of 3D carousels: the back faces of cards. The solution is dual-sided matched texturing, ensuring that looking from inside or outside the ring displays the exact same upright card—no frame ever displays mirrored or inverted content across a full revolution.

styles.label: Carousel 3D
styles.description: Eight cards sit on a circular ring laid out with sin and cos, spinning through exactly one full revolution while each card billboards outward with matched front and back faces so it never reads as mirrored or upside down.

cards.name: chart-live-moves
cards.summary: Three data-driven motions: a live oscilloscope trace, dots regrouping into a figure, and an axis forced to rescale.
cards.use: Data storytelling segments; respectively conveying "real-time aliveness," "every data point is a person," and "growth that cannot be contained"
cards.energy: Medium-high (data as drama)
cards.intention: Charts are not illustrations—they are the narrative. A shared prerequisite across all three variants (production testing precedent): **authentic chart context is mandatory**—authentic axis labels, authentic data, authentic copy; grayscale placeholder bars fail to convey data storytelling power. Variant A Oscilloscope stream: the curve write head is pinned to the right edge oscillating up and down, while historical data streams off the left frame edge, interrupted by a sudden burst spike (amplitude 2.2x, readout jumps larger in accent color)—"real-time" needs no words, and events happen live. Variant B Unit dot swarm regroup: 320 dots (~40 renders per dot) disperse -> cluster into three swarms (floating authentic labels: Promo, Launch film, Explainer) -> march into bar columns (authentic axis markers) -> assemble into a large dot-matrix numeral "12,847"—the exact same dots throughout, allowing viewers to trace an individual dot joining the formation. Variant C Axis rescale shock: line climbs normally, then new values punch through the chart ceiling boundary by 226px (a thick accent line impaling the title area and crashing into top-right KPI numbers), pauses half a beat, and the y-axis dramatically rescales (old ticks fly out / new ticks slide in / grid lines densify / old line flattens into the horizon), with new values dropping into place alongside authentic value tags—enacting growth as "the axis cannot hold it."

styles.label: Oscilloscope Stream
styles.description: A live curve writes itself in at the right edge with sudden spikes, then brakes to a true standstill.
styles.use: Monitoring / real-time products: a living, breathing system

styles.label: Unit Dot Swarm Regroup
styles.description: A dot swarm migrates in three staggered spring acts and finally regroups into a number.
styles.use: User scale / composition narrative: "every dot is a person"

styles.label: Axis Rescale Shock
styles.description: A new value bursts 220px out of the chart frame, forcing the axis to rescale: ticks swap, the grid densifies, the old line flattens.
styles.use: Growth curve highlight: literal "off the charts" moment

cards.name: chip-grid-single-select-blackout
cards.summary: Five option chips fade in, then a single grey press frame flashes before the chosen chip turns solid black with a tiny bounce while the others drop to eighteen percent without moving.
cards.use: Interactive demonstration for single-select, subscription plan, or tier selection; causal shots showing "what happens after selecting this"; pricing and checkout parameter flows
cards.energy: Medium-Low (the sole burst is that single grey flash frame; everything else is restrained)
cards.intention: A 1-frame grey flash + 3-frame invert-to-black breaks down the two distinct states of real UI `:active -> :selected` into an explicit performance. Viewers see "finger presses" followed by "system confirms," rather than a vague gradient fade. The remaining chips drop to 18% opacity while their **positions remain strictly locked**: once rearranged, viewers will assume the page refreshed, destroying the semantics of "single selection."

styles.label: Chip Grid Single Select Blackout
styles.description: Five option chips fade in, then a single grey press frame flashes before the chosen chip turns solid black with a tiny bounce while the others drop to eighteen percent without moving.

cards.name: circle-match-iris
cards.summary: An iris expands from a circular UI element and lands on a matching circle in the next scene.
cards.use: Seams between scenes where the foreground has a circular element (avatar/icon/circular button) and the background has a circular hero subject (donut chart/circular progress ring); transition technique card.
cards.duration: 5.5s / 165f (entrance + focal lock 40f + anticipation 7f + circle match & iris bloom 37f + sweep 58f + static hold 47f).
cards.energy: Medium-high
cards.intention: A standard iris wipe opens from an arbitrary point on screen, communicating nothing more to the audience than "the page changed." This card fuses the iris wipe with a **match cut**: the iris must detonate outward from the exact center of a **real circular element** in the foreground, expanding to reveal a circular chart in the incoming scene that anchors onto that exact same circle. The audience perceives that "the avatar circle transformed into the chart circle," allowing the geometry itself to carry the narrative progression (this person → this person's metrics). This is the UI-native realization of the match cut: grounded not in visual coincidence, but in semantic circle-to-circle alignment. Like the travel transition trio, the incoming scene is pre-present within the outgoing foreground, but anchored by an abstract geometry rather than a container.

styles.label: Circle Match Iris
styles.description: An iris expands from a circular UI element and lands on a matching circle in the next scene.

cards.name: cloner-depth-echo
cards.summary: A card duplicates into a diagonal depth trail, holds briefly, then accelerates back into one springy original.
cards.use: Value props of "multiple replicas / multi-tenancy / scale / batch processing"; one-shot demonstration of "one = many."
cards.energy: Medium (Display-and-collapse cadence)
cards.intention: A UI translation of the Spline/C4D Cloner vocabulary: a hero card instantly duplicates 7 translucent clones stepping backward along the Z axis (250px spacing, opacity decaying from 100% to 28%, distant clones reducing to wire outlines), popping out in a staggered column; holds for ~32f allowing viewers to register "there are many"; then all clones ease-in rapidly back into the hero card, collapsing into one with a 1.06x impact bounce. The demo ties "one = many" to a concrete feature: 1 video-shotcraft render card (launch-film) × 8 shot variations; upon collapse, 8 shot indicator dots at card base illuminate simultaneously as headline lands: "One prompt. / Eight shots." Distinct from parallax in depth-layer-moves (which layers different content): this is an equidistant echo array of the **exact same content**, conveying scale rather than spatial navigation.

styles.label: Cloner Depth Echo
styles.description: A card duplicates into a diagonal depth trail, holds briefly, then accelerates back into one springy original.

cards.name: collab-cursor-moves
cards.summary: A five-cursor ensemble drifting and typing across a shared board as living collaboration ambience.
cards.use: Canvas scenes with collaboration/multiplayer themes, establishing an ambient warmth of "team presence" across the frame
cards.energy: A Low-Medium (ambient layer, can underpin any duration)
cards.intention: Most cursor cards in the library are "functional clicks" (cursor-flyover is a single-cursor click-and-tour). This card elevates collaborative cursors with identity nameplates into **actors**: five cursors enter staggered and drift continuously as ambient particles, carrying the entire feeling of "team presence," with one pausing to type (a cameo role). SVG cursors + nameplate chips come at very low cost with high narrative density, serving as the most cost-effective visual proof for collaboration themes.

styles.label: Cast Ensemble
styles.description: Five named cursors spring in staggered, drift on sine paths, one types a cameo line, and the whole cast gathers to watch at the end.
styles.use: Canvas / whiteboard products ambient layer: background vitality showing others collaborating

cards.name: countdown-arc-scatter
cards.summary: Numbers arranged tangentially along a large arc sweep past and brake to a stop, the winning digit sliding out of the dial to become the first character of the headline.
cards.use: Countdown/time-commitment copy ("5 min to install"); data reveal moments; short light-background shots requiring an "instrument dial" vocabulary
cards.duration: ~3.3s (100f@30fps: dial sweep ~30f + landing 20f + headline assembly + hold 22f; can be compressed to 33f single-shot minimum)
cards.energy: High (large 96° sweep compressed into ~20 frames, pure impact)
cards.intention: Writing "installs in 5 minutes" as a static title card carries zero credibility. Sweeping an instrument dial places this number into a **scale**: 45, 35, 28, 22, 17, 10 sweep past and brake hard at 5 — the audience sees a decline "from a lot down to very little," where the number proves its own claim. After stopping, "5" does not vanish; instead, it **translates directly to become the first character of the headline**. Having a single element transition seamlessly from gauge to copy is the highest-value technique in this card.

styles.label: Countdown Arc Scatter
styles.description: Numbers arranged tangentially along a large arc sweep past and brake to a stop, the winning digit sliding out of the dial to become the first character of the headline.

cards.name: crane-rise-reveal
cards.summary: The camera starts tight on one data row, rises and pulls back, then reveals a full dashboard filling the frame.
cards.use: Establishing shot transitioning "from detail to global view"; inverse counterpart to drone-dive-landing (global -> single point dive)
cards.energy: Medium-High (continuous unidirectional motion, no impact beat)
cards.intention: The library already contains drone-dive-landing for opening establishing shots—slamming into a hero close-up from a bird's-eye perspective ("global -> focus"). This card is its exact mirror: "focus -> global"—first zooming tight onto a single row of real data so viewers parse "what this is," then rising and pulling back like a crane arm as row after row floods into view, until the full product dashboard covers the screen—"the row you just saw is merely one cell in this entire wall." Suited for openings spotlighting product scale and content richness; choose only one direction per film.

styles.label: Crane Rise Reveal
styles.description: The camera starts tight on one data row, rises and pulls back, then reveals a full dashboard filling the frame.

cards.name: crash-zoom-punch
cards.summary: A six-frame push races from a wide view to a target close-up, ending with either an elastic overshoot or a heavy impact stop.
cards.use: Feature section "calling out" shot—pins the viewer's gaze instantly onto the target card/module; use impact stop for highest emphasis level
cards.duration: ~0.5s action + holds before and after (6–11f action, hold >=30f before to establish overview, hold >=45f after to read close-up)
cards.energy: High (instant impact, not sustained high energy)
cards.intention: A slow push-in (spotlight-hero-card) says "please look", while a crash zoom says "LOOK AT THIS!"—slamming from overview to close-up in a single beat, leaving the viewer no choice. Landing styles come in two variants: elastic rebound conveys bounce ("look here"), while impact shake conveys weight ("this is the one"), chosen by emphasis level.

styles.label: Crash Zoom Punch
styles.description: A six-frame push races from a wide view to a target close-up, ending with either an elastic overshoot or a heavy impact stop.

cards.name: cursor-flyover
cards.summary: After an overview fade-in the camera flies to each of four screen corners in turn while an SVG cursor arrives with it, pointing and leaving a click ripple at every stop.
cards.use: Feature tour of a single-page product: takes the audience through four feature areas in one continuous shot, using the cursor as a "tour guide finger"
cards.duration: ~8.0s (240f@30fps; overview 22f, four stops 44f each (flight 20f + hold 24f), pull-back 24f, hold 18f)
cards.energy: Medium (equidistant cruise, rhythmic clicks and ripples setting the cadence)
cards.intention: A shot-saving alternative to "four separate cuts for four features": one continuous camera threads four corners into a single visitor route, with the cursor acting as the viewer's attention proxy—wherever it moves and clicks, the viewer looks. Spatial continuity naturally helps the audience remember the spatial relationships between features.

styles.label: Cursor Flyover
styles.description: After an overview fade-in the camera flies to each of four screen corners in turn while an SVG cursor arrives with it, pointing and leaving a click ripple at every stop.

cards.name: dataviz-landscape-open
cards.summary: Streams of light merge across a dark data landscape while labels hover and a shallow-depth camera glides forward.
cards.use: Brand-level abstract opening ("data universe" metaphor), leading into light-themed product segments or wordmark; division of labor with glow-flyline-moves: that card handles connecting line narratives between cards within a segment, while this card is a full-frame landscape dedicated to openings
cards.duration: 5–8s (opening ambient segment, <=1 time per film; demo 180f)
cards.energy: Low start building slowly (starting position, preserving room for subsequent ascent)
cards.intention: A brand-level opening category proven by the Linear Releases launch film: framing the data universe behind the product as a **dark-stage landscape**—tributary light bundles converging from screen depths into a central trunk (metaphor for "countless workflows merging into one product"). Realism stems from three pillars: (1) Fictional issue/task ID tags floating along lines (demo uses video-shotcraft shot numbers + camera move names: each tributary represents a shot merging into a finished film), prompting viewers to recognize "that's what I see every day"; (2) Heavy depth of field—foreground sweeping past in heavy blur, midground tags crisp and legible, background fading into haze, with three-tier depth transforming flat SVG into physical space; (3) Slow, steady camera flyover—this is an ambient establishing sequence rather than a technical showcase; leave high velocity for later shots.

styles.label: Dataviz Landscape Open
styles.description: Streams of light merge across a dark data landscape while labels hover and a shallow-depth camera glides forward.

cards.name: deck-deal-flyin
cards.summary: A physical card stack opens the scene, then cards accelerate into a live grid as the camera follows the growing page.
cards.use: Showcasing list views and card walls with high content volume and continuous incoming streams; establishing immediate impressions of information density.
cards.duration: 150f (~5s: 0–36 deck close-up + anticipation, 36–~101 dealing, 108–150 full board hold)
cards.energy: High (Workhorse for rhythm ramp-up sections; avoid placing as opening shot)
cards.intention: Present suspense first (what is this stack?), then reveal the payoff (it is dozens of items flying into the page to take their places). Viewers must feel items streaming in endlessly, with each card snapping into position with urgent momentum.

styles.label: Deck Deal Flyin
styles.description: A physical card stack opens the scene, then cards accelerate into a live grid as the camera follows the growing page.

cards.name: depth-layer-moves
cards.summary: Layered parallax rails: three speed tiers slide past to build depth, and the hero floats up as the rail settles.
cards.use: Sections where flat screenshots need "physical depth": card groups, lists, or horizontal page tours
cards.energy: Medium (tactile quality)
cards.intention: Panning an entire page is "looking at a page"; layered depth is "standing inside the page's space." Parallax rails add depth to horizontal panning (the Disney multiplane camera principle, matching Linear promo aesthetics).

styles.label: Multiplane
styles.description: A multiplane parallax dolly: three layers slide at different speeds, pulling depth out of flat screenshots.

cards.name: doc-park-left-pill-deal
cards.summary: The source document slides left until only a sliver remains and keeps scrolling slowly, while three outlined pills are dealt one at a time, each followed by a caption that darkens word by word.
cards.use: Voiceover-driven sections presenting analytical conclusions one by one; core explanatory shot for document understanding, recommendation reasoning, or review critique products.
cards.energy: Low (Deliberate dealing cadence without peaks; maintains visual vitality via continuous background auto-scroll)
cards.intention: Conclusions must be delivered one by one for audiences to absorb them. But fading out the source document leaves conclusions floating in a vacuum—viewers lose track of where the findings originate. This card's solution is **keeping the source document in frame**: it parks against the left edge with only a sliver exposed, scrolling slowly (signaling it is actively being parsed), while each conclusion pill on the right branches directly from this source. The dealing cadence is deliberately measured to provide ample time for the voiceover to complete each sentence.

styles.label: Doc Park Left Pill Deal
styles.description: The source document slides left until only a sliver remains and keeps scrolling slowly, while three outlined pills are dealt one at a time, each followed by a caption that darkens word by word.

cards.name: document-typewriter-reveal
cards.summary: A fully typeset document writes itself behind one accent-color caret, opens both side columns, and drops history entries into the rail.
cards.use: Feature shots for document/report/note products; the single beat with the highest information density
cards.duration: 150f (~5s, including history-list-stack tail and slogan hold)
cards.energy: Low-medium (highest information density, paced steadily so viewers can read text)
cards.intention: The audience will read every word on screen — this shot's persuasive power rests entirely on the conviction that "the document is real." Typewriter-style composition turns a static page into an "actively authored document," while history entries dropping into the sidebar add temporal depth representing continuous output.

styles.label: Document Typewriter Reveal
styles.description: A fully typeset document writes itself behind one accent-color caret, opens both side columns, and drops history entries into the rail.

cards.name: draw-svg-trace
cards.summary: An ink stroke traces an element outline, closes with a dark flash, and hands focus to the revealed content.
cards.use: Calling attention to a single card, chart, or title during entrance; element-level technique (full-page blueprint tracing belongs to wall-reveal-moves Variant B).
cards.duration: 132f (anticipation 10f + trace 40f + dark flash handoff 16f + underline 18f + hold 40f, ~4.4s)
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intention: "Drawing into existence" is the most natural entrance metaphor in ink-and-paper aesthetics: elements do not fly or fade in, but are sketched on the spot by an invisible pen. While wall-reveal-moves Variant B provides a full-page blueprint version (drawing fullscreen wireframes in segments before lighting up regions), this card serves as its **element-level close-up variant**—a single stroke, a single subject, a single closure with visible pen tip and clear direction, tailor-made for callout moments highlighting "what we discuss next." Its secondary application is title underline growth: the same 18f shorthand technique delivering a hand-drawn stroke under key terms, sharing aesthetic DNA with marker pen tokens.

styles.label: Draw Svg Trace
styles.description: An ink stroke traces an element outline, closes with a dark flash, and hands focus to the revealed content.

cards.name: element-body-moves
cards.summary: A contact shadow that separates during lift, giving interface elements physical weight.
cards.use: Providing physical presence beyond mere positional changes; establishing tangible proof of card hovering during 2.5D camera moves and card callouts.
cards.energy: Variant A Low-Medium
cards.intention: Motion cards in the library typically govern "changing positions"—fly-in, slide, bounce, while the elements themselves remain rigid bodies. This card governs **changing physical presence**: providing credible proof of hovering—as a card lifts, its contact shadow directly underneath simultaneously enlarges and diffuses, lifting paper off the surface to support 2.5D camera moves with physical staging. Unlike CameraMotionBlur (which handles shutter streaks), surface lift represents bodily depth.

styles.label: Contact Shadow Lift
styles.description: A card lifts off the page with a growing, fading contact shadow beneath, then drops back with a tiny squash.
styles.use: Sequential card callout emphasis; 2.5D layer elevation buildup

cards.name: flying-words
cards.summary: Keywords spawn deep in a perspective tunnel and rush past the camera along the z axis, fading in and out on a lifecycle curve across two seamless loops.
cards.use: Dynamic background for keyword clouds / capability catalogs; high-information bottom layer for openers and closers; transitions requiring depth-travel sensation
cards.energy: High (continuous full-screen 3D translation, never static)
cards.intention: The crudest way to list keywords is piling them into a static word cloud. The word tunnel spreads those same terms **across the time axis**: spawning in the distance, scaling up, and sweeping past the lens to vanish. The audience only actively reads three to five words at any moment, yet the subjective impression is "an enormous wealth of concepts." It serves as a background layer, not the hero — with the camera stationary and elements moving, layering a headline or UI foreground on top causes zero visual conflict. Replacing the word list with project-specific keywords requires zero changes to the underlying motion logic.

styles.label: Flying Words
styles.description: Keywords spawn deep in a perspective tunnel and rush past the camera along the z axis, fading in and out on a lifecycle curve across two seamless loops.

cards.name: fracture
cards.summary: Twenty-five 3D tiles fly in from scattered space and lock into a poster in a center-out ripple, hold for a beat, then accelerate outward off-screen in all directions.
cards.use: Opening establishing shot for brand/poster reveals "from chaos to formation"; reversing or isolating the second half functions as a hard transition
cards.energy: High (high energy at both ends, calm in the middle; ideal for locking to BGM accent beats)
cards.intention: Framing "product formation" as a physical event: fragments carry individual rotations out of 3D space and fly into position, letting viewers watch a coherent visual emerge from disorder; after holding to read copy, the entire assembly detonates off-screen, cleanly handing attention to the next shot. Symmetrical entry and exit allows the asset to run forward or reversed.

styles.label: Fracture
styles.description: Twenty-five 3D tiles fly in from scattered space and lock into a poster in a center-out ripple, hold for a beat, then accelerate outward off-screen in all directions.

cards.name: fui-hud-moves
cards.summary: A reticle that assembles itself around a target and locks on.
cards.use: Calling attention to any target element (replacing red arrows and circles without freezing the frame)
cards.energy: Medium-high (lock-on frame serves as impact beat)
cards.intention: A versatile motif borrowed from sci-fi fictional UI (Jarvis / Territory): in-motion target acquisition. Four L-shaped corner brackets rush in from off-screen, overshoot and rebound, then snap firmly into place around the target element accompanied by a popping label—division of labor with freeze-annotate: that card freezes the screen for annotations, whereas this card singles out targets mid-flow.

styles.label: Reticle Lock On
styles.description: Four corner brackets fly in and clamp onto the target with an overshoot snap; the target brightens and its label pops.
styles.use: Target callout; landing on heavy sound effect beat

cards.name: gauge-readout-moves
cards.summary: Two instrument reads: a full-range needle self-test and a moving scale that races beneath a fixed pointer.
cards.use: Dashboard opening ceremonies or performance metric reveals; Variant A for multi-dial startup feeling, Variant B for large single-metric leaps
cards.energy: Medium-high (mechanical ceremony)
cards.intention: Turning "reporting a number" into the physical behavior of an instrument: Variant A is an automotive ignition self-test—three side-by-side dials on a card sweep their needles across the full 270 deg arc in a swift whoosh, lighting swept tick marks in sequence, then spring back to settle on authentic values in a staggered wave; values beneath each dial pop on the settle frame, presenting the full range before reporting the metric to create an opening statement of power. Variant B uses aircraft airspeed tape syntax—the readout window and indicator needle remain pinned to the screen centerline, while a full-height scale tape scrolls from behind the window, first creeping against an old upper limit, breaking through to sprint (peaking at ~100px/f), and concluding with a spring-braked rebound: "the world moves, the needle stays," converting numeric magnitude into tangible displacement distance.

styles.label: Needle Sweep Selftest
styles.description: Ignition self-test: gauge needles slam to full arc, then swing back with overshoot to their true values, staggered across dials.
styles.use: Dashboard opening / system readiness ceremony

styles.label: Tape Scroll Fixed Pointer
styles.description: The pointer holds still while a long scale tape crawls, sprints at 45px/f, and spring-brakes onto the final reading.
styles.use: Single metric major jump (performance doubled / quota increased)

cards.name: glass-pill-dictation-typing
cards.summary: A fixed-width glass pill pops in slightly oversized and settles, glowing with an accent gradient inside that fades out as a placeholder sentence types across it.
cards.use: Entrance for voice/AI input pills; interactive cue shots for "speak to it"; a quiet transitional beat between high-energy sequences
cards.energy: Low (the quietest beat in the video; only light receding)
cards.intention: Telling a subtle story through "light receding as input occurs": on standby it glows (waiting for you to speak), and the moment you speak it yields that light to text. Across 3.3s it performs only three actions: pop in, type, and light recedes. Any superfluous action (bouncing, color morphing, icon animations) destroys its function as a musical rest.

styles.label: Glass Pill Dictation Typing
styles.description: A fixed-width glass pill pops in slightly oversized and settles, glowing with an accent gradient inside that fades out as a placeholder sentence types across it.

cards.name: glitch-cycle
cards.summary: Status phrases cycle through one monospace slot, each dissolving into noise at both ends with RGB split and jitter, while a progress bar tracks the whole run.
cards.use: Status reporting during load/build/deploy processes; technical intro "system self-diagnostics"; rhythmic background beds pushing time forward with a machine tone
cards.duration: ~5.6s (168f@30fps; 38f per phrase in demo, with final phrase extending to shot end as hold)
cards.energy: Medium-high (continuous high-frequency noise pulses, peaking at transitions)
cards.intention: The clumsiest approach to status logs is fading in four lines of text one by one. Cycling compresses them into **a single slot**: phrases fuse into glitch at both ends and solidify in between, remaining pristine with only occasional single-character twitches in the middle — the audience reads "the system is advancing step-by-step," rather than four disconnected lines of copy. Glitch intensity is this card's grammar: dense = switching states, faint = dwelling in the current state. A bottom progress bar stitches the four beats into a cohesive timeline, while the final phrase settles probability to zero, concluding upon rest.

styles.label: Glitch Cycle
styles.description: Status phrases cycle through one monospace slot, each dissolving into noise at both ends with RGB split and jitter, while a progress bar tracks the whole run.

cards.name: glow-flyline-moves
cards.summary: Three dark-scene accents: ambient glow orbs, connecting flight arcs, and a synchronized orb-to-line relay.
cards.use: Atmosphere and data storytelling for the sole dark-scene sequence in a video: use A for ambient bed, B for data flow, C for background reacting to foreground; Linear landing page aesthetic
cards.energy: A Low (ambient floor) / B Medium / C Medium-high
cards.intention: The library's first card built entirely within a **dark environment**. The precedent that "brightening is invisible on white backgrounds" conversely implies: to play with light, step into the dark first. Variant A provides spatial breathing—three large ambient glow orbs drift organically across a dark canvas, swimming behind a central frosted glass card and tinting through the glass, while card edges catch glow as orbs approach, keeping the background alive. Variant B delivers data verbs—luminous arcs strike from Card A to Card B with bright leading heads and fading comet trails, pulsing target outlines upon arrival to give metric relationships directional intent. Variant C solders A and B together—as a flight line lands, the adjacent background glow orb surges in brightness on the exact same frame; atmospheric and event layers **resonate on the same frame**, conversing rather than acting independently (combination critical point: decoupling the resonance frame degrades the effect into two disjointed cards).

styles.label: Glow Orb Ambient
styles.description: Three huge blurred glow orbs drift on twin sine paths, driving edge-light on nearby cards by distance.
styles.use: Dark scene backdrop layer; card breathing ambience

styles.label: Flyline Arc
styles.description: A glowing head draws a bezier flyline between cards in 22 frames, the tail fading behind it; the endpoint pulses on arrival.
styles.use: Data flow / metric association; dashboard narrative

styles.label: Orb Flyline Relay
styles.description: Orbs and flylines welded together: a background orb surges on the exact frame its flyline lands, so backdrop answers foreground.
styles.use: Dark scene highlight; three-card relay convergence

cards.name: gradient-transition
cards.summary: The background morphs smoothly through linear, radial, and conic CSS gradients — angle, color stops, center, and radius each interpolated per-parameter with narrow cross-fades between types.
cards.use: Continuous variation for atmospheric backdrops or chapter background colors; provides a "living" background layer for static typographic segments.
cards.energy: Low (pure background motion, yielding to foreground content).
cards.intention: Gradients are not static textures, but animateable parameter sets: within the same gradient type, every parameter can be interpolated to create fluid, continuous movement, while transitions across different types are seamlessly bridged using short cross-fades. Designed as a background layer, this card infuses segments that lack hero foreground action with a steady, low-velocity hum of ambient energy.

styles.label: Gradient Transition
styles.description: The background morphs smoothly through linear, radial, and conic CSS gradients — angle, color stops, center, and radius each interpolated per-parameter with narrow cross-fades between types.

cards.name: gradient-word-sweep
cards.summary: A gradient light sweeps left to right across a keyword, charging each character with glow that decays behind the wavefront until the whole word breathes.
cards.use: Charging a single verb / value-prop word in a slogan (Supercharged / faster / AI…); typography centerpiece in high-energy segments; slogan frame in dark-field brand films
cards.duration: Sweep charge ~15–20f (must be fast) + steady-state lightning breathing 1–2s; full shot 2.5–3.5s
cards.energy: High (single-word explosive beat, preceding and following elements should yield)
cards.intention: Within a sentence of white text, only the keyword gets "energized": colorful gradient light sweeps across characters from left to right like an energy injection — brightest at the instant of sweep (the wavefront wake), decaying into a steady state; once filled, fine branching lightning arcs between characters while the word breathes in soft glow. Three critical rules: **Fast** (sweep charge takes 15–20f; any slower reads as a progress bar), **Wavefront brightest** (freshly ignited characters exhibit the strongest effect, without which the gradient is a static wipe), **Restrained bloom** (AE-style multi-layer glow without devolving into a muddy blob; lightning must stay fine and sparse as an accent).

styles.label: Gradient Word Sweep
styles.description: A gradient light sweeps left to right across a keyword, charging each character with glow that decays behind the wavefront until the whole word breathes.

cards.name: grain-dissolve
cards.summary: A clean line of text boils into displaced grain noise inside a hatched selection frame, then the particle cloud condenses into a larger glowing wordmark that locks sharp.
cards.use: Concluding "XX. Now Live" launch announcements; energy-concentrating beats condensing sentence-level information into a brand shortmark
cards.duration: ~2.0s (60f@30fps; grain burst 0.26–0.56s, condensation 1.2–1.42s, solidifying settle resolution)
cards.energy: Medium-high (short, singular energy pulse; natural outro synchronization beat)
cards.intention: Filming "distilling a sentence into a single word" as a physical event: the sentence destabilizes and boils into particles (dissolution of information), the selection bounding box implies "actively selecting and extracting," and then all particle energy collapses inward into a larger, brighter short wordmark—the audience registers that "all of this culminates in this."

styles.label: Grain Dissolve
styles.description: A clean line of text boils into displaced grain noise inside a hatched selection frame, then the particle cloud condenses into a larger glowing wordmark that locks sharp.

cards.name: graze-face-tour
cards.summary: The camera skims low across the UI surface like terrain while page text hovers above the interface and settles down as the shot advances.
cards.use: Feature area tour (skimming UI like terrain); paired with dark stages + neon rim lights for a product "inner world" sequence; UI content appearing zone by zone
cards.duration: Single segment 4–5s; can extend via multi-segment relays
cards.energy: Medium-high (continuous camera advance + sequential element landings, high information density)
cards.intention: Filming UI as landscape: a steep-angle close-up turns sidebar trees, navigation bars, and list rows into passing terrain, while shallow depth of field reinforces "surface skimming." The dramatic focal point is **text settling onto the page from above**: text/components do not fade in on the spot, but hover above the interface (lifted along the 3D z-axis), casting matching soft shadows onto the surface while aloft; as the camera advances, they accelerate downward and settle, with shadows converging and vanishing with height—the audience watches the interface "complete itself" as the camera glides by. The shadow is essential: without a shadow, hovering reads as a generic translation entrance; with a shadow, the spatial relationship snaps into place instantly.

styles.label: Graze Face Tour
styles.description: The camera skims low across the UI surface like terrain while page text hovers above the interface and settles down as the shot advances.

cards.name: hashtag-to-pill-materialize
cards.summary: A typed "#word" hard-cuts into a wide pill tag, holds, shrinks into its slot on the page, then hard-cuts again to reveal the finished view.
cards.use: Demonstration segments for tagging, categorization, and keyword features (tagging in note apps, topic aggregation); three-stage narrative of "input -> transform into UI entity -> settle into final product"
cards.duration: 120f (4s) — typing ~40f + hard-cut pill hold ~18f + shrink-move ~14f + post-reveal rest ~1.2s (original video 18–21.5s)
cards.energy: Medium (crisp and decisive; derives punch from hard cuts rather than bouncy springs)
cards.intention: The conventional technique for turning text into entities is gradient/morph/expand. Frame-by-frame breakdown of the original video proves Bear does the opposite: **materialization is a 1-frame hard cut**—one frame text + cursor, the very next frame a complete pill, with zero expansion, zero cross-fade, zero rebound. A hard cut delivers the certainty of "snap, done"; any gradient softens an "entity" into a "special effect." The backbone of the entire shot is **one slide sandwiched between two hard cuts**: hard cut materialization -> smooth shrink-move settling -> hard cut reveal of finished page. The sole continuous motion (shrink-move) is framed between two hard cuts, rendering it fast yet grounded. This rhythmic backbone is essential; altering the character of any of the three stages (replacing hard cuts with fades, or slide with cuts) collapses the shot.

styles.label: Hashtag To Pill Materialize
styles.description: A typed "#word" hard-cuts into a wide pill tag, holds, shrinks into its slot on the page, then hard-cuts again to reveal the finished view.

cards.name: icon-field-colorize
cards.summary: A grid of grayscale icons staggers in to fill the screen, holds a beat, then brand-color bands ripple down and light the whole field at once.
cards.use: Opening sequence laying out product capabilities (icons = functional universe) before flooding with brand color; feature showcase pages, ecosystem/integration scale overviews, lead-in before opening logo
cards.duration: Entrance ~45f stagger + hold ~10f + color flip 12–45f + terminal hold; total segment 3–6s (demo 170f: color flip 30f tier + title lockup + terminal hold 1s)
cards.energy: Medium (entrance is build-up; color flip instant is the sole burst)
cards.intention: Establishing sheer abundance with grayscale first—hundreds of small icons stagger into the frame, with grayscale ensuring they read as ambient background texture without stealing focus; holding for a beat lets viewers register "the screen is packed," followed by brand color sweeping downward in rapid horizontal waves, illuminating the grey world in an instant. The linchpin is that **colorization is not a simultaneous hard cut across frames**: analysis of the original video proves multiple color waves sweep downward within ~0.5s (blue blankets the field first, followed by orange/green/red covering lower tiers), settling into a layered four-color horizon—the wave provides velocity and direction, whereas a raw cut merely reads like changing slides.

styles.label: Icon Field Colorize
styles.description: A grid of grayscale icons staggers in to fill the screen, holds a beat, then brand-color bands ripple down and light the whole field at once.

cards.name: icon-performance-moves
cards.summary: An escalating attention bounce that compresses on landing to call the eye to an icon.
cards.use: Half-screen close-up icon showcases; introducing new features
cards.energy: Anticipation build-up
cards.intention: The first entry in the library's icon animation category: the icon acts as a focal performer under a tight camera, not a passive UI micro-interaction in a corner. Attention-bounce borrows from the macOS Dock vernacular—the video-shotcraft app icon inside the Dock bounces 4 times in place, leaping higher each time (0.35 -> 1.2x icon height), compressing on each landing (final bounce: width 1.2x, height 0.8x) with ripple droplets. Neighboring icons rack-focus out of blur, and on the highest leap the camera gently pushes in 8% (drawn toward it). Once settled, a "New in Shotcraft" feature panel springs open—cutting "user attention" directly into the narrative.

styles.label: Attention Bounce
styles.description: An icon bounces with growing height, squashing on each landing with dust puffs, until the camera leans in and a panel pops.
styles.use: Feature introduction: "look at me" -> camera leans in -> panel pops

cards.name: impact-feedback
cards.summary: Two impact layers: a combo counter with damage feedback, and a full anime-style impact frame.
cards.use: The "hit instant" when elements slam into place or collide—adding arcade-grade juice to drops and crash stops; select variant along the intensity ladder
cards.duration: n/a (element-level technique piggybacking on landing actions; frame budgets detailed in parameter table)
cards.energy: High (instantaneous impact)
cards.intention: When elements slam into place without a tactile "impact moment," landings feel like bland slide-deck fly-ins. Game juice (Vlambeer's screen-shake philosophy) and anime impact frames offer the same answer: bite into time during those few hit frames to transmit kinetic impulse to the viewer. The two variants form an intensity ladder: Variant B uses local freeze frames layered with damage numbers and jumping combo counters, turning a feature list into a fighting-game combo with strong narrative clarity; Variant C delivers the heaviest punch—a 3f negative color inversion with radiating focus lines upon crash-stop, representing the highest, most stylized emphasis.

styles.label: Hit Counter
styles.description: Three cards slam in one after another; every hit freezes 2 frames, floats damage digits, and bumps the combo counter.
styles.use: Feature point combo sequence: "many features" told as combo hits with arcade feel

styles.label: Anime Impact
styles.description: On the crash-zoom stop: 3 frames of full-screen negative, radial speed lines, and red-cyan fringing, all gone by frame 4.
styles.use: Sole climax punch of the video; peak emphasis level

cards.name: integration-hub-map
cards.summary: A page flips 180 degrees into an integration hub where five app icons pop in together and rainbow light tubes connect with pulses flowing through them.
cards.use: Integration and ecosystem showcase sections (one product connecting everything); version overhaul narratives (legacy page flipping to new page); dark neon aesthetic feature climaxes.
cards.duration: Anticipation ~0.5s + fast flip ~1.2s + simultaneous icons pop -> light tubes connect across two beats ~0.7s + pulse breathing ≥1.5s; full segment 4.5–5s
cards.energy: Medium-High (Flip is the explosive peak, pulse flow is the lingering resonance)
cards.intention: Flipping a page represents "entering a new era": the old document page rotates a full 180° to reveal the new hub page—it must be a complete flip rather than an angle tilt, executing as a **fast flip with a deceleration tail** in a single continuous movement without mid-way stalls (users interpret "uniform" as unbroken momentum rather than literal linear timing; stopping at the 90° edge was rejected). The edge profile only flashes briefly (1–3f pulse; prolonged bloom plates were rejected). Integration executes across **two beats**: five icons pop in on the exact same frame (beat one) → five light tubes draw and connect simultaneously on the same frame (beat two)—synchronicity is essential to convey "ecosystem ready at once"; staggered connections read like piecemeal negotiations (rejected in two review rounds). Once connected, bright pulses circulate along light tubes from icons toward the central hub; continuous "throughput" gives life to the final state.

styles.label: Integration Hub Map
styles.description: A page flips 180 degrees into an integration hub where five app icons pop in together and rainbow light tubes connect with pulses flowing through them.

cards.name: lead-word-zoom-assemble
cards.summary: The lead word fills the frame at 2.3x and keeps drifting toward the viewer, then a single curve recedes it to size while the line slides left and the trailing words are pushed into their slots — pivoting on the lead word centre and the measured baseline.
cards.use: "Introducing" title cards for brand/product names; keynote-style opening second shot; single-sentence claims requiring "let one word fill the frame first, then assemble the full sentence"
cards.duration: ~2.8s (84f@30fps; sentence assembled at f36, shift up and subtitle at f32–46, hold 26f, final 12f crash)
cards.energy: Medium-high (opens with frame-filling large type, but features only one motion arc throughout with no secondary shock)
cards.intention: The most common mistake with title cards is fading in the entire sentence at once — the viewer receives five words simultaneously and remembers none of them. This card turns reading order into a **physical sequence**: first showing a single word so massive it fills the frame while continuously pushing toward the viewer, forcing them to read it; then that word recedes to its final scale and position within the sentence as the rest of the line grows around it. By the time it settles, the viewer has registered the key term twice. The true secret to the tactile feel is not the easing curve, but the **pivot anchor**. As the lead word travels from screen center to the third character position in the row, anchoring `transform-origin` at the row box center causes scaling and sliding to pull the text in opposing directions, producing visible baseline jitter in the final frames. Anchoring `transform-origin` horizontally at the lead word's center and vertically at the baseline locks those two coordinates completely, ensuring the row merely recedes in size with zero wobble.

styles.label: Lead Word Zoom Assemble
styles.description: The lead word fills the frame at 2.3x and keeps drifting toward the viewer, then a single curve recedes it to size while the line slides left and the trailing words are pushed into their slots — pivoting on the lead word centre and the measured baseline.

cards.name: letterspace-materialize
cards.summary: Every letter of a widely tracked wordmark draws itself in parallel, growing like handwriting and finishing together on the same frame.
cards.use: Opening or closing brand wordmark reveals (wide tracking, thin skeleton wordmarks; demo uses video-shotcraft lowercase); chapter title cards; closing frames requiring serenity and premium restraint
cards.energy: Low (serene ritual, completes in a single breath)
cards.intention: The wordmark neither fades in nor types out; rather, it "crystallizes": the strokes of all letters begin growing simultaneously, as if an invisible hand were writing every letter at once, finishing together in the exact same frame. Two critical requirements: **continuity** (strokes must be drawn continuously without segmented masking—drawing half then another half reveals the trick; every intermediate frame must look like "halfway written"); **synchronicity** (all letters begin and end in the same frame—letter-by-letter stagger carries typewriter semantics, whereas here it conveys holistic brand ritual).

styles.label: Letterspace Materialize
styles.description: Every letter of a widely tracked wordmark draws itself in parallel, growing like handwriting and finishing together on the same frame.

cards.name: light-play-moves
cards.summary: Two controlled light effects: a spotlight sweep that reveals the title and a single sheen pass across a card.
cards.use: Treating light as an expressive brushstroke (sweeping / brushing): dark title reveals (A), crowning hero cards (B)
cards.energy: A Medium / B Low
cards.intention: The library previously treated "light" solely through spotlight-hero-card as a single pin-point highlight. These two variants systematize light into two brushstrokes with distinct responsibilities: Variant A is **sweeping**—a swinging conical beam illuminates a headline that is barely visible in the dark, lighting up wherever it travels (distinguished from spotlight-hero-card, which highlights a card, whereas this sweeps text); Variant B is **brushing**—a 45 deg specular sheen glides gently across a deep ink hero card once, clipped by rounded corners as a silent coronation. All variations require dark canvases or dark hero elements—**brightening is invisible on white backgrounds** (precedent), which serves as the bedrock of this entire card.

styles.label: Spotlight Sweep
styles.description: Two copies of the text: a dim one always on, a bright one revealed by a radial mask that sweeps twice before locking fully lit.
styles.use: Dark scene giant title reveal opening

styles.label: Sheen Sweep
styles.description: A single 45-degree highlight band sweeps once across a dark card, clipped by its rounded corners.
styles.use: Single coronation pass on a resting hero card

cards.name: line-carry-transition
cards.summary: A progress line exits scene A, guides the camera sideways, then turns corners to become the frame of scene B.
cards.use: Transitions between two scenes with graphical kinship (progress bar → card frame, underline → chart axis); marquee transition position in a promo video, evoking the graphic relay of the Catch Me If You Can title sequence.
cards.duration: ~6.3s / 190f (progress bar fills 36f + breakout 10f + lateral pan 56f + frame wrap 24f + in-frame poster 30f + static hold 24f).
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intention: The three major families in the transition library (travel / hidden cut / block push) all answer the question of "how to swap scenes." This card's answer is: **do not swap at all—let a single line guide you across**. Once a progress bar fills to 100%, its leading tip extends past the card edge and punches out of the frame. The camera tracks the line laterally across 1920px into a new world. In transit, the line turns right angles to construct the card frame of Scene B. The frame closes, content fades in, and from start to finish the viewer's eyes never leave the line. Graphic continuity *is* the transition. Contrast with a match cut: a match cut aligns shapes across an edit point—it is still an edit; this is continuous drawing—**there is no cut**. The line's identity must possess narrative logic (the progress bar has "completed," so it extends outward); a line without motivation is merely arbitrary decoration.

styles.label: Line Carry Transition
styles.description: A progress line exits scene A, guides the camera sideways, then turns corners to become the frame of scene B.

cards.name: list-reveal
cards.summary: Menu rows scale into place one after another with a faint overshoot while the whole list drifts slowly upward, keeping the per-item entrance and the group motion on two independent layers.
cards.use: Navigation, sidebar, and settings panel entrances; UI sections where "interfaces self-assemble"; also serves as low-energy background during voiceover setup.
cards.energy: Low (Steady cadence without peaks; maintains visual vitality via upward drift)
cards.intention: Staggered list item fade-ins are easily prone to feeling stiff: each item freezes once it finishes moving, leaving the screen completely dead between arrivals. This card's solution adds a slow drift to the container that is completely independent of the per-item entrances—individual rows "find their slots" while the whole list "breathes." Viewers clearly read each item while no single frame across the entire shot is frozen solid.

styles.label: List Reveal
styles.description: Menu rows scale into place one after another with a faint overshoot while the whole list drifts slowly upward, keeping the per-item entrance and the group motion on two independent layers.

cards.name: list-stack-press
cards.summary: List cards fly up from below, compress the growing stack on every landing, and advance a synchronized counter.
cards.use: Feeds, radars, and inbox shots conveying "fresh incoming items daily"; asset lists emphasizing cumulative growth.
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intention: "Stacks possess physical weight": each time a new card lands, the existing stack depresses and springs back—viewers perceive from physical feedback that "these items are tangible assets accumulating over time." A synchronized counter increments on each landing, reinforcing the sense of volume.

styles.label: List Stack Press
styles.description: List cards fly up from below, compress the growing stack on every landing, and advance a synchronized counter.

cards.name: logo-shrink-wordmark-lockup
cards.summary: A neon slit ring shrinks fast into a solid white O with an overshoot brake, slides left to make room, letters stagger in one by one, and an accent slogan fades in below.
cards.use: Outro brand lockup: collapsing full-screen visual energy into a standard "icon + wordmark + tagline" lockup
cards.energy: Medium (impactful collapse phase resolving into steady settling cadence)
