cards.intention: The outro's signature stamping ceremony: a full-screen neon ring collapses with kinetic energy into a compact icon, healing its split gap and turning solid white (transitioning from show mode to standard brand identity), then steps through standard lockup assembly—icon steps left, wordmark glides in letter by letter, and tagline resolves below. The audience sees the brand "settle firmly" out of pure motion.

styles.label: Logo Shrink Wordmark Lockup
styles.description: A neon slit ring shrinks fast into a solid white O with an overshoot brake, slides left to make room, letters stagger in one by one, and an accent slogan fades in below.

cards.name: magician-card-flourish
cards.summary: A blue starburst flashes on black for a third of a second, then a card shoots out of the flash, spinning along an arc toward camera before freezing near full frame.
cards.use: Magical entrance for single cards, posters, or covers (opening key visual, hero product card reveal); pure dark stage; visual burst requiring "summoned from thin air" theatricality
cards.energy: High (singular burst beat; completely still after freeze)
cards.intention: A magician flourishing a card: a blue starburst flashes, and a card appears summoned from the light—catapulting from infinite distance at frame center (visually a pinpoint), spinning rapidly along an arc toward the camera, and hard-freezing the instant it reaches center into a near full-frame showcase. Three critical magical pillars: **flash leads** (light is the summoning ritual, lasting a crisp 0.3s), **catapult rhythm** (slow-in anticipation -> burst acceleration -> decelerating arc), and **freeze to stillness** (zero deceleration tail, zero rebound; 13 exact rotations guarantee facing camera upon freeze).

styles.label: Magician Card Flourish
styles.description: A blue starburst flashes on black for a third of a second, then a card shoots out of the flash, spinning along an arc toward camera before freezing near full frame.

cards.name: marker-underline-title
cards.summary: After the headline settles, a marker stroke draws itself under the keyword — tapered, rough-edged, and slightly tilted to follow the italic.
cards.use: Emphasizing a single keyword in a headline (new / free / AI…); brand tone with handcrafted/human warmth; editorial annotation-style emphasis
cards.duration: Starts +4–8f after headline settles, draws in 8–12f, total 1–1.5s
cards.energy: Low (single-stroke flourish, does not compete with headline)
cards.intention: A hand-drawn marker stroke suddenly appears beneath printed headline typography, using textural contrast to pull a single word out of the composition — like someone circling a key point on a printed poster. Three critical rules: **Fast** (drawn in 8–12f in a single continuous stroke; any slower reads as a progress bar), **Close** (hugging the text baseline; too far away reads as a divider line rather than emphasis), **Following letter posture** (the stroke beneath italic text must tilt slightly upward from lower-left to upper-right — drawing the tilt in reverse is the most common and immediately fake mistake; see Known Pitfalls).

styles.label: Marker Underline Title
styles.description: After the headline settles, a marker stroke draws itself under the keyword — tapered, rough-edged, and slightly tilted to follow the italic.

cards.name: mosaic-reframe
cards.summary: Twelve tiles morph continuously between a regular grid, a feature mosaic with one hero slot, and a rotated diagonal cascade, each tile interpolating position and size independently with a slight stagger.
cards.use: Display transition demonstrating "multiple ways of viewing the same content": showcase of layout versatility for portfolio, template library, or photo gallery products.
cards.duration: Approx. 7.1s (214f@30fps; emerge 0–22f · hold A · A→B 56–92f · hold B · B→C 132–176f · hold C through 214f).
cards.energy: Medium (continuously flowing rearrangement, no jarring burst, composed and confident demeanor).
cards.intention: Let the audience witness "layout itself thinking": the exact same twelve pieces of content transform from an orderly archival state (regular grid) into an editorial hierarchy (feature mosaic), and finally into a dynamic, expressive composition (diagonal cascade).

styles.label: Mosaic Reframe
styles.description: Twelve tiles morph continuously between a regular grid, a feature mosaic with one hero slot, and a rotated diagonal cascade, each tile interpolating position and size independently with a slight stagger.

cards.name: neon-frame-forerun
cards.summary: A neon frame races ahead to outline the scene in steep perspective while components drop from above and the page brightens as they land.
cards.use: Ceremonial entrance for UI panels in dark brand films (frame arrives first, content drops in after); debut of primary feature sections; openers for neon/cyber aesthetics.
cards.duration: Frame trace ~0.7s + brighten & drop ~2.7s + background extinction settle ~1s; full segment 4–4.7s (demo 140f)
cards.energy: Medium-High (Three layered motions compounding, all serving a unified entrance)
cards.intention: Frame first, fill second: the neon outline races around the boundary like runway lights to stake out real estate, proclaiming "content is arriving here." As the page brightens from pitch black inside the frame, components drop in from above with shadows—viewers watch the interface being seated into the frame. The three motion layers (frame trace / page illumination / component drop) must **lock into tight synchronization**: component landing progresses in lockstep with page illumination, concluding slightly after, with frame glow merging into panel rim glow. Background neon tube echoes extinguish during the final phase, handing full luminosity to the hero element.

styles.label: Neon Frame Forerun
styles.description: A neon frame races ahead to outline the scene in steep perspective while components drop from above and the page brightens as they land.

cards.name: neon-frame-orbit-drop
cards.summary: After a neon frame draws itself, the camera arcs left to right while every page component drops from the air and lands on the same frame.
cards.use: Grand single-take reveal for a single-page UI (contrasting with sectional tours); hero visual unveiling in dark neon aesthetics; sibling shot to neon-frame-forerun.
cards.duration: Frame trace ~0.5s + rotation & simultaneous drop ~2.5s + settle ~1s; full segment ~4.7s (140f, rotation settles at 128f followed by rest)
cards.energy: Medium-High (A singular sweeping gesture, settling into complete stillness)
cards.intention: Twin variant to neon-frame-forerun: similarly uses frame-first, content-after structure, but the camera is not static—it sweeps in a continuous arc from the page's left flank to the right flank, while all components drop from the air simultaneously during rotation. The non-negotiable rule is **simultaneous landing**: every component and text block launches on the same frame, descends on the same frame, lands on the same frame, and drops shadows in perfect synchrony—this is the visual syntax of a "monolithic entrance" (review ruling: staggered version rejected as "all components and text should drop from the air and land together"). Staggered landings belong to walkthrough shots (graze-face-tour); revealing an entire page in a single beat requires synchronous landing, and the two timing vocabularies must never be conflated.

styles.label: Neon Frame Orbit Drop
styles.description: After a neon frame draws itself, the camera arcs left to right while every page component drops from the air and lands on the same frame.

cards.name: neon-triple-marquee
cards.summary: Three rows of outlined neon giants scroll in opposite directions across the full screen, lighting up in turn on a one-third phase offset.
cards.use: Outro theme word repetition sections; shooting the "lingering resonance" of a three-word slogan; background musical sequences without voiceover
cards.duration: 4–5s (demo 150f: 18f staggered ignition + loop body + 18f staggered power-off + 8f dark hold)
cards.energy: Medium-high (continuous flow + sequential pulses, no abrupt impacts)
cards.intention: A single marquee line is merely web decoration; stacking three lines in counter-directions and cycling luminance in phase becomes "theme words marching in review before the audience." The critical core is **alternating illumination**: at any given moment, only one line is the neon protagonist, while the other two recede into subtle stroked silhouettes—all three blazing at once is a signage malfunction; rotating illumination is a recap. Counter-scrolling creates an "immersive enclosure": top and bottom rows roll right while the middle row rolls left, pinning the viewer's gaze in between as words stream continuously from both edges, conveying "there is no end to these three principles."

styles.label: Neon Triple Marquee
styles.description: Three rows of outlined neon giants scroll in opposite directions across the full screen, lighting up in turn on a one-third phase offset.

cards.name: orbit-ring-title-open
cards.summary: Eight 16:9 content cards orbit an ellipse at a constant rate with their contents frozen on the first frame, then all start playing together while the centred headline de-blurs into place and a marker block sweeps across the key phrase.
cards.use: Opening establishing shot = "this product offers an entire ecosystem"; flagship showcase for asset libraries, template hubs, feature matrices, or case studies; grounds a central claim with authentic living product visuals rather than a static grid of screenshots
cards.duration: 150f (5s@30fps; marker block settles at f64 followed by 2.9s steady orbit + slow push-in; HANDOFF_EXIT triggers exit handoff from f118)
cards.energy: Medium (constant orbit is the sole ongoing motion; marker sweep is the single punch beat)
cards.intention: When opening with "we offer an entire suite," the common approach arranges screenshots into a grid—yet grids are static, reading as "a pile of pictures" rather than "a living product." This card transforms display into an **orbital carousel**: eight cards orbit an ellipse at constant speed, with cards perpetually entering and leaving the frame, implying "there is always more," while the headline anchors immovably in the center. The key design choice is that **card contents must truly play**. Static screenshots on a ring look like a generic carousel; running authentic animations turns the ring into "products actively working." However, eight cards playing immediately would overwhelm viewer attention—so cards are **frozen on their initial frame** during entrance, beginning playback in unison only after the ring expands and the headline commences. Viewers first recognize a ring of product surfaces -> read the headline -> then discover all cards are alive.

styles.label: Orbit Ring Title Open
styles.description: Eight 16:9 content cards orbit an ellipse at a constant rate with their contents frozen on the first frame, then all start playing together while the centred headline de-blurs into place and a marker block sweeps across the key phrase.

cards.name: outline-word-fill
cards.summary: An outlined word snaps down from triple size while a dashed circle and horizontal guides close in, then the stroke flips to solid white in a single frame with one brief glow.
cards.use: Heavyweight hammer beats for single-word value propositions / slogans; anchor shots aligned with rhythm drops; emphasis frames in dark-field brand videos
cards.energy: High (3.2x contraction + instantaneous ignition, brief high impact)
cards.intention: Driving a word home like a hammered nail does not rely on a slow fade-in, but on **two successive landings**: first, an enormous hollow outlined word rapidly contracts into place (the landing of size); second, the thin stroke snaps into solid white within a single frame (the landing of texture). The intervening 1.5s of contracting dashed circles and extending horizontal guides represents an "aiming" sequence — technical drafting vocabulary that frames the ignition beat as a decisive "confirmation." Fill **must be instantaneous**: a slow wipe fill degrades an impactful hammer blow into a leisurely cosmetic animation.

styles.label: Outline Word Fill
styles.description: An outlined word snaps down from triple size while a dashed circle and horizontal guides close in, then the stroke flips to solid white in a single frame with one brief glow.

cards.name: outro-group-photo-launch
cards.summary: Elements from the film assemble around the wordmark as a crane settle, stage light, and gold dust create a launch-event finale.
cards.use: Outro / brand finale; "family portrait" closing shot for multi-feature products
cards.energy: Peak (highest energy point of the entire video)
cards.intention: Recalling one representative element from every featured function for a group photo, with the wordmark taking center stage as the grand finale—before exiting, the audience remembers that "all of these capabilities belong to a single product." Execution must be keynote-grade: energy pushed to the absolute peak of the video.

styles.label: Outro Group Photo Launch
styles.description: Elements from the film assemble around the wordmark as a crane settle, stage light, and gold dust create a launch-event finale.

cards.name: overhead-camera-moves
cards.summary: Two overhead reveals: a tilted scene leveling into view, and a tabletop layout dropping sharply into place.
cards.use: Opening or transition storytelling via pitch angles: use Variant A for single-page establishing shots, and Variant B for multi-page inspections diving into a chosen page
cards.energy: A Medium / B Medium-high
cards.intention: Overhead perspective has been a gap in the shot library: crane-rise is a "pan + zoom" elevation with a fixed tilt angle, while space-camera Variant C (drone-dive) is a one-way dive landing. These two recipes let the **pitch angle itself tell the story**: Variant A is a reveal—the entire page lies flat under rotateX; at opening, only a luminous perspective sliver at the far top edge is visible (like first light on the horizon), then the camera tilts up to level the page as content pours into view like unrolling architectural plans on a table; Variant B is a selection—three page cards lie flat in a tabletop layout, the overhead camera slides horizontally across them (Wes Anderson tabletop style), then dives steeply into the chosen page, leveling it to full screen: "inspect the field, pick this one." Selection guide: use A for single-page openings; use B for multi-page transitions or openings.

styles.label: Tilt Reveal
styles.description: The whole page lies flat at -80 degrees and tilts upright in one 43-frame ease-out with a slight overshoot at the end.
styles.use: Opening establishing shot; single hero subject

styles.label: Overhead Tabletop Drop
styles.description: A card array lies at 62 degrees overhead; the camera pans across the tabletop, then dives and lands on the layout.
styles.use: Multi-page overview followed by selection; dual transition / opening use

cards.name: page-turn-transitions
cards.summary: A full-page transition where the old page splits open like double doors to reveal the new one.
cards.use: Chapter-level page transitions: "turning the page" ritual between two major narrative movements; distinct division of labor from the shot-transitions family (camera handoffs)—where that family represents "the drone moving across," this represents "the page itself being a physical slab."
cards.duration: Single variant 150f (prior state establishment 30–40f + transition 24–40f + follow-through and settle ≥70f), approx. 5.0s.
cards.energy: Medium-high
cards.intention: The three shot-transitions variants and transition-travel/hidden-cut all treat the page as a "scene"—the camera moves between environments. This card treats the page as a **physical entity**: it possesses thickness, mass, and can split apart. The physical slab metaphor imparts a heavier ceremonial weight, tailored for chapter-level page transitions (concluding Feature A → introducing Feature B) rather than shot-level continuity handoffs. The double-door barn split represents "the old yielding to the new"—the outgoing page tears open down the center and slides apart, while the incoming page ascends from beneath, suggesting supersession and replacement.

styles.label: Barn Door Split
styles.description: The old page splits into two halves that accelerate out to both sides, edges glowing, while the new page rises to meet the gap.
styles.use: Old vs new transition: redesign comparison, Plan A -> Plan B

cards.name: page-waterfall-wall
cards.summary: Real page captures flow at different speeds across a tilted 3D wall, creating an endless field of content.
cards.use: Showcasing scale across "multiple pages / features / templates"; montage mid-sections or post-intro product breadth showcases.
cards.energy: Medium (Flowing showcase type)
cards.intention: A flowing overview: lets viewers absorb dozens of pages streaming past within seconds, communicating sheer scale rather than individual detail. Division with outro-group-photo-launch: that is a **converging** overview (elements fly in to frame the wordmark for a final portrait, conveying "all part of one unified product"), whereas this card is a **flowing** overview (content streams continuously without freezing, conveying "vast volume yet to explore"). Division with wall-reveal-moves: that is a wall **entrance action**, whereas this card represents a wall's **continuous state**; an entrance card can hand off to this card to continue streaming.

styles.label: Page Waterfall Wall
styles.description: Real page captures flow at different speeds across a tilted 3D wall, creating an endless field of content.

cards.name: panel-grid-moves
cards.summary: An angled comic-panel split that cuts one moment into three framings before resolving to a poster.
cards.use: Using panel splits as a metronome: slicing multiple angles of the same subject into frozen panels on the beat; hitting rhythm points
cards.duration: 156f ≈ 5.2s (full-screen 3/4 angle 20f + 3 slash-cut freeze panels + screen engulf + poster hold)
cards.energy: Medium-high
cards.intention: Distinction from `wall-reveal-moves`: that card addresses "how an entire wall enters" (one-time reveal), whereas this card addresses "how panel grids act as a rhythm engine"—splits land on musical beats, and panel transitions serve as drum kicks. Variant A splits: the screen is slashed by three diagonal seams, freezing three camera angles of the same product simultaneously; after a resting beat, the final panel sweeps across to engulf the full canvas—drawing on the split-screen comic vernacular of Scott Pilgrim. Ideal for multi-angle product showcases (demo: a prime lens engraved with video-shotcraft, three commentary panels numbered "Shot 01 / 02 / 03," resolving into a "Craft the shot." poster after the screen sweep).

styles.label: Comic Panel Split
styles.description: Three slanted comic panels show the same subject at three zooms, popping in 2 frames apart, each slowly pushing until the last panel eats the screen.
styles.use: Multi-angle views of the same subject; graphic novel pacing

cards.name: paper-title-card
cards.summary: A sentence stamps onto paper word by word, highlights one amber italic term, and closes with a short rule.
cards.use: Chapter transitions / value-proposition title cards; introductory cards preceding major feature reveals; breathing spaces throughout full videos
cards.energy: Low (breathing beat, separating high-energy sequences)
cards.intention: Offers the audience a one-sentence breather between product feature sequences, clearly communicating "what you will see next and why it matters." The letterpress stamping tactile texture unites the title card with paper-and-ink product interfaces in the same visual world.

styles.label: Paper Title Card
styles.description: A sentence stamps onto paper word by word, highlights one amber italic term, and closes with a short rule.

cards.name: picker-carousel-feature-cycle
cards.summary: A vertical mobile-style picker holds its focus pill still while the list passes through it, each item decelerating hard into place and resting for several frames before the next.
cards.use: List shots reading out feature names or use cases sequentially; interactive demonstrations of "picking one option"; showcasing picker-style controls in mobile products
cards.energy: Medium (every snap serves as a beat marker, advancing at a steady 5-beat pace)
cards.intention: Crafting the physical sensation of "selection": the focus frame remains stationary while content rolls through and snaps into place. Each item must **truly pause for several frames** upon stopping—continuous scrolling reads like a loading animation, while pauses convey "this item is selected." Distance attenuation (simultaneous decay across opacity, font size, and grayscale) is the sole method to keep viewer gaze locked onto the center row.

styles.label: Picker Carousel Feature Cycle
styles.description: A vertical mobile-style picker holds its focus pill still while the list passes through it, each item decelerating hard into place and resting for several frames before the next.

cards.name: pill-chip-slot-cycle-handled
cards.summary: A dark chip inside the sentence rolls through feature words, its width easing to each word so the surrounding text is pushed apart while grey ghost items show above and below.
cards.use: "We handle your ___" value proposition copy; concluding punchlines for SaaS capability enumerations; primary hero moments in light-background brand videos
cards.duration: ~5.0s (150f@30fps: static hold → 3 transitions (0.25/0.47/0.69) → ending static hold)
cards.energy: Medium (steady 3-beat rhythm, width expansion/contraction is the sole continuous motion)
cards.intention: Word slot cycling divides into two schools: insulating the sentence from change (fixed-width reels), or forcing the sentence to **accept** change (capsule expands, pushing adjacent words outward). This card chooses the latter: the cost is requiring precise width calculations, but the reward is a living sentence — "Your" and "Handled" get physically pushed aside, making the audience feel the tangible weight of words within the chip. Grey ghost items revealed above and below serve as a secondary signature: explicitly indicating "this is a scrollable list," setting viewer expectations for subsequent terms.

styles.label: Pill Chip Slot Cycle Handled
styles.description: A dark chip inside the sentence rolls through feature words, its width easing to each word so the surrounding text is pushed apart while grey ghost items show above and below.

cards.name: pill-slot-cycle
cards.summary: A fixed sentence keeps its trailing pill slot spinning like a slot machine through feature words until the final word locks the sentence.
cards.use: The most elegant solution for feature enumerations (faster than itemized lists, more semantic than character reels); one-sentence value props with multiple verb phrases
cards.duration: Entrance 12f + 21f per beat × word count + resolution 14f + hold; 6 words ≈6.7s (demo 200f, including 48f complete sentence hold)
cards.energy: Medium (steady metronome, no peak)
cards.intention: Listing six capabilities with an itemized list requires six rows, taking six beats of sequential fades that consume the entire screen. Word slot cycling condenses them into **a single slot within a single sentence**: the sentence stem "One skill to ___" (in demo: Storyboard it → Capture the page → Move the camera → Cut on the beat → Design the sound → Render the film) is the promise, each rolling pill badge in the slot is proof, and finally the pill launches away as "do it all." locks into place — evidence completed, conclusion stamped. The structure carries an innate three-act narrative: promise → enumeration → resolution. The critical requirement is that the sentence stem **remains completely motionless**: the viewer's eyes stay locked on the slot; any movement in the stem scatters the sense of enumeration.

styles.label: Pill Slot Cycle
styles.description: A fixed sentence keeps its trailing pill slot spinning like a slot machine through feature words until the final word locks the sentence.

cards.name: print-texture-transitions
cards.summary: A print-based reveal: ink bleeding outward from a drop point to consume the old scene.
cards.use: Paper-and-ink aesthetic choices for scene change seams; the third family alongside camera handoffs and travel moves—"medium development" transitions.
cards.energy: Medium (gradual manifestation, no jarring impact beat).
cards.intention: Existing transition grammar already includes camera handoffs (the three shot-transitions variants) and spatial travel (transition-travel), both rooted in spatial/optical metaphors. This technique introduces a third family: **medium metaphors**—the new visual is not "arriving" through motion, but is being "printed and dyed" into reality. It taps directly into the physical imagination of the library's paper-and-ink aesthetic: an ink drop landing on rice paper, bleeding outward with feathery tendrils to consume the prior scene in an organic, writerly fashion. For films with an inherent paper/ink sensibility, this serves as an organic alternative to light-leak-burn (accent-color light leaks) within the "medium-based" seam category.

styles.label: Ink Bleed Reveal
styles.description: A print-based reveal: ink bleeding outward from a drop point to consume the old scene.
styles.use: Scene replacement with editorial texture and narrative tone

cards.name: product-card-progressive-assemble
cards.summary: A product card builds itself field by field as image, title and pills pop in, the old price gets struck through while an accent new price springs out, and highlighter blocks sweep across the copy.
cards.use: Capability showcases on product/item detail views; primary shot for narratives around "structured extraction," "autofill," and "data assembling itself."
cards.energy: Medium (Dense sequence of micro-events without a single explosion; maintains forward momentum via continuous slow camera push)
cards.intention: Fading in a detail card directly merely tells viewers "here is a card." Assembling it field by field transforms the card into a **form actively being filled in real time**: as each field snaps into position, the viewer's attention is guided step by step through the card's information architecture—where the image lives, where the title is, where the price sits, and where body highlights lie. Price strikethrough downgrade is the sole semantic event in the entire sequence (representing a transformation rather than a mere appearance), which is why it is staged at the most prominent position mid-sequence.

styles.label: Product Card Progressive Assemble
styles.description: A product card builds itself field by field as image, title and pills pop in, the old price gets struck through while an accent new price springs out, and highlighter blocks sweep across the copy.

cards.name: quad-split-parallel-scenes
cards.summary: The frame hard-cuts into a 2×2 grid where four micro-scenes run in parallel — typing, a whip zoom, word pops, and a cursor interaction chain — with every beat offset by a few frames.
cards.use: Montage beats in rhythmic sections conveying "many features running concurrently"; peak density moments in trailer midsections
cards.duration: 90f (3s @ 30fps: 0–62f parallel bombardment + 28f final hold, zero transitions throughout)
cards.energy: High (four parallel threads + staggered beat impacts, textbook BGM chorus placement)
cards.intention: Substitute parallel density for sequential showcases: four events unfold simultaneously before the viewer's eyes. Audiences cannot read every detail line-by-line, but because one quadrant "acts" every 3–6 frames, the scanning rhythm is gripped tight. This is a methodology card: all in-panel content is replaceable—the staggered beat choreography is the true recipe.

styles.label: Quad Split Parallel Scenes
styles.description: The frame hard-cuts into a 2×2 grid where four micro-scenes run in parallel — typing, a whip zoom, word pops, and a cursor interaction chain — with every beat offset by a few frames.

cards.name: radial-ripple-phone-chips
cards.summary: Four concentric grey circles breathe out of phase like water ripples while a centered phone mockup auto-scrolls its feed and two white feature chips spring in and hover.
cards.use: The "here it is" hero freeze-frame for mobile products; feature breakdown sections flanking both sides; opening or closing product overviews
cards.energy: Low (serene, breathing feel, sustained by the continuous ripple motion to keep the shot alive)
cards.intention: Anchor a mobile phone at screen center with minimal motion while keeping it undeniably "alive": concentric circles provide atmospheric breathing, in-screen auto-scrolling proves "live content is running inside," and flanking chips highlight feature names. All three motion layers run at deliberate, slow paces, combining so the composition never feels frozen—the gold standard for product hero beauty shots.

styles.label: Radial Ripple Phone Chips
styles.description: Four concentric grey circles breathe out of phase like water ripples while a centered phone mockup auto-scrolls its feed and two white feature chips spring in and hover.

cards.name: radial-wave
cards.summary: A 17x9 dot grid lights up in rings that spread outward from the center, each dot overshooting its scale before settling into a steady glow, then a brighter pulse collapses back inward from the edges.
cards.use: "System power-on" beat for product/brand openings; establishing shot for data grids, node maps, and network coverage narratives.
cards.energy: Medium-High (Punchy opening burst, settling into steady low-energy ambient base post-wavefront)
cards.intention: Transforms the static fact that "many points exist simultaneously" into the dynamic narrative that "energy expands outward from a single source to the entire system." Viewers perceive not a static grid, but an electrification event: center ignites first, radiance ripples across like water waves, settling into an illuminated state—setting the stage for subsequent content. The secondary inward wave serves as an acknowledgement pulse, signaling that the system is responsive.

styles.label: Radial Wave
styles.description: A 17x9 dot grid lights up in rings that spread outward from the center, each dot overshooting its scale before settling into a steady glow, then a brighter pulse collapses back inward from the edges.

cards.name: research-card-stack-scroll
cards.summary: Dark paper cards drop into the center every twelve frames and pile along a downward-right axis, squashing on landing while only the topmost card renders its full text as the rest blur into the stack.
cards.use: Communicating scale for "processing vast literature / ingesting massive document volumes"; capability shot for research, search, and batch-processing products.
cards.energy: Medium-High (Uniform high-frequency cadence without single explosions, maintaining steady pressure)
cards.intention: The message to deliver is "volume," but presenting 13 cards simultaneously reads as an impenetrable wall. Restructuring into an assembly pipeline: cards arrive one by one, each actively read (the top card always renders complete text), and once parsed, sink into the pile with increasing blur. Viewers perceive a continuous processing throughput rather than a static stack. The background grid sliding downward at matching velocity provides velocity reference—without it, accumulation reads as "cards shrinking in place."

styles.label: Research Card Stack Scroll
styles.description: Dark paper cards drop into the center every twelve frames and pile along a downward-right axis, squashing on landing while only the topmost card renders its full text as the rest blur into the stack.

cards.name: rhythm-interrupt-moves
cards.summary: Stepped punch-in jump cuts that break cadence on the same frame.
cards.use: Using "broken continuity" itself as a rhythm engine: stuttered punch-ins (A); complementary to beat-cut-moves (cut placement)
cards.energy: A Medium
cards.intention: Rhythm cards in the library typically govern "how to cut, and how densely to cut"; this card governs **how to break cadence**—viewers anticipate continuity, and breaking that expectation becomes the expression: Variant A breaks space—three zero-tween magnification jumps within the same framing (1x -> 1.6x -> 2.6x), channeling the staccato cadence of Godard jump cuts to deliver the commanding instruction of "look here, closer, that's it" far more forcefully than a continuous camera push. Ideal for forcing attention onto critical metrics.

styles.label: Jump Cut Punch In
styles.description: Three zoom steps with zero tweening, origin pinned on the target, each jump landing with a darkening pulse like a tick.
styles.use: Stepped zoom-in on core metric; documentary-style focus

cards.name: riso-print-hits
cards.summary: A risograph impact: a single misregistered colour split that snaps into alignment.
cards.use: Emphasis hit for titles and cards, serving as an ink-and-paper analog to digital glitch flashes; 1–2 standalone climax hits per video
cards.energy: High
cards.intention: RGB chromatic aberration glitch flashes (part of impact-feedback Variant C) belong to the language of phosphor screens, conflicting with paper-and-ink aesthetics. This card provides a printmaking equivalent: the element splits into two monochrome risograph printing plates (demo: fluorescent pink x blue; using `multiply` for physical ink depth rather than `screen` fluorescence, blending into dark ink when aligned), mimicking an off-register risograph that shakes before snapping sharply into perfect registration—delivering identical impact while grounding physical imagination in ink on paper. Single hit: splitting on crash stop, damped oscillation, hard cut into alignment, stamping authority onto a key landing. Demo features a two-color riso promotional poster for video-shotcraft ("CRAFT IT / LOUD." + 3-column feature highlights, with monochrome engraved mark at stamp center).

styles.label: Misregistration Hit
styles.description: The title slams in and splits into two color plates offset 32px, oscillating down until they snap back into register with a scale pulse.
styles.use: One or two stamp impacts in video; moment title or big type locks in

cards.name: row-embed
cards.summary: Content rows descend with perspective, flatten into the page, and flash a thin amber seam at the moment of insertion.
cards.use: Detail and list views where "structured data roots into the page"; batch entrances for row-level content.
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intention: Rows in a detail view do not merely "appear"—they "grow into" the interface. Each row descends from mid-air and seats seamlessly into the page layout, with an accent-colored seam flashing at the instant of insertion acting as a visual onomatopoeia for a mechanical "click."

styles.label: Row Embed
styles.description: Content rows descend with perspective, flatten into the page, and flash a thin amber seam at the moment of insertion.

cards.name: sakuga-timing-shift
cards.summary: Movement begins in stepped, held drawings and suddenly switches to frame-by-frame acceleration at the climax.
cards.use: Emphatic displacement of single elements (card entries, metrics crossing finish lines); sequences requiring contrast between "handcrafted stutter" and "explosive climax"
cards.energy: Medium-high
cards.intention: The library's timeline manipulation already includes speed-ramp-freeze's freeze-unfreeze and hit-counter's local hit-stops. This card represents a different axis—**altering frame rate rather than velocity**: The stuttered phase uses quantized driving frames `q = floor(f/3) * 3`, moving only once every 3 frames (10fps flipbook animation); at the transition frame, it switches instantly to raw frame `f` continuous motion for a silky sprint. The blunt cadence of shooting on 3s cuts against the fluidity of shooting on 1s on the same screen, channeling the timing direction of Japanese sakuga animation. The stuttered phase does not convey poor quality but handcrafted craft, and the switch point marks the climax.

styles.label: Sakuga Timing Shift
styles.description: Movement begins in stepped, held drawings and suddenly switches to frame-by-frame acceleration at the climax.

cards.name: scan-bracket-sweep
cards.summary: A skeleton document pops to center, black L-shaped framing brackets drop into its corners, and a thin line with a gradient trail sweeps up and down across it five times.
cards.use: Process shots depicting "analyzing / verifying this document"; capability demos for document products; mid-funnel sequences in upload-to-analysis pipelines
cards.energy: Medium-low (mechanical, restrained, rhythm carried entirely by the breathing of reciprocating passes)
cards.intention: Help viewers comprehend that "this asset is being inspected line by line by a machine." Framing brackets box the target first (declaring the object of inspection), and a scanning light band traverses the full layout back and forth (declaring the inspection process). The key requirement is that **the document itself remains completely motionless**: if the document also moves, viewers cannot distinguish whether it is "being analyzed" or "loading."

styles.label: Scan Bracket Sweep
styles.description: A skeleton document pops to center, black L-shaped framing brackets drop into its corners, and a thin line with a gradient trail sweeps up and down across it five times.

cards.name: scanline-annotate-focus
cards.summary: A bright scanline travels down the page and, as it clears each block, camera framing brackets snap inward onto that region and a monospace caption types out beside it.
cards.use: Analytical shots showing "AI reading your page or brand"; breakdowns of design systems and brand guidelines; product self-explanation sequences
cards.energy: Medium (mechanically calm, paced by constant scanline movement, annotations serving as cadence beats)
cards.intention: Turn the abstract concept of "analysis" into a visible chain of cause and effect: wherever the scanline travels, that section is framed and named. Viewers follow the "machine's gaze," which demands a constant scanline speed and annotations strictly lagging behind the scanline's passage—**scan first, frame second**. Disrupting this order turns an analytical process into a staged animation.

styles.label: Scanline Annotate Focus
styles.description: A bright scanline travels down the page and, as it clears each block, camera framing brackets snap inward onto that region and a monospace caption types out beside it.

cards.name: scanline-assemble-flyin
cards.summary: The page starts as an empty dark grid; a scanline descends and each component flies in from off-screen to snap into place behind it, with motion blur and a bright edge flash on landing.
cards.use: Openings where a "page generates itself"; core capability demos for AI website builders and automated layout tools; capability narratives from blank canvas to finished product
cards.energy: Medium-high (scanline remains steady, but each incoming component delivers an impact beat with rising density)
cards.intention: Provide a credible construction sequence for "generating a page": the scanline acts as a construction progress bar, and components flying in from off-screen serve as construction actions. The golden rule is that **the scanline completes its pass on the exact frame the final component snaps into place**—finishing the scanline early or letting component arrivals drag out destroys the causal link of "scanning drives assembly."

styles.label: Scanline Assemble Flyin
styles.description: The page starts as an empty dark grid; a scanline descends and each component flies in from off-screen to snap into place behind it, with motion blur and a bright edge flash on landing.

cards.name: scroll-brake-moves
cards.summary: Two fast-scroll stops: a long page decelerating precisely onto a target, and the same stop paired with a locking reticle.
cards.use: Changelog, release history, or long list sections: "we ship continuously, and today's entry is the biggest"; use Variant B when the stop requires higher impact
cards.energy: High start, medium resolution (speed-contrast profile)
cards.intention: Linear changelog video grammar: an entire year's release log rushes past as a long ribbon at high speed (smearing into a colored band), then exponentially decelerates with razor precision onto the current release entry, which lifts off the page surface, highlights, and dims surrounding items—density says "we never stop shipping," while the abrupt brake says "today's release is the monumental one." Variant B is a compound mutation: on the **exact same frame** the scroll brakes, four L-brackets fly in from offscreen and clamp onto the target entry—the thud of the brake and the click of the clamp resonate on the exact same frame (composite requirement: bracket takeoff frame must match the list's initial halt frame; offsetting them degrades it into two uncoordinated effects).

styles.label: Changelog Scroll Brake
styles.description: A 2400px scroll decelerates exponentially over 50 frames, motion blur driven by per-frame speed, and the target row lifts lit while the rest dim.
styles.use: Changelog segment baseline

styles.label: Brake Reticle Lock
styles.description: The scroll overshoots 30px past the target and springs back, and on the brake frame corner brackets fly in and bite with a popping label.
styles.use: Highlight segment requiring punchy landing impact

cards.name: segmented-thumb-hero
cards.summary: An oversized segmented control gets a close-up: a cursor slides in, presses, and the white thumb snaps to the other segment as icons swap with a spring.
cards.use: Announcement shot for "mode switch / binary choice" features (e.g., video-shotcraft Prompt->Film, Chat->Agent); macro shot where a single UI micro-interaction sustains an entire shot
cards.duration: ~3.5s (demo 110f: float-in 18f + cursor 24f + click + slide 8f + icon pop + hold)
cards.energy: Medium (micro-interaction close-up; refined without overpowering)
cards.intention: When switching to a new product mode, conventional shots replace the entire screen. This card does the inverse: magnifying a segmented control to 1080px wide in extreme close-up, where **the 8-frame thumb displacement itself is the narrative**—"we crossed from A to B." Without surrounding page context, the control becomes the stage. The causal chain is complete: cursor glides in (someone arrived) -> press + ripple (decision made) -> thumb slides (world responds) -> new icon pops up (new identity established). All four beats are essential: omitting the cursor makes the UI move itself; omitting the icon pop leaves the switch unrewarded.

styles.label: Segmented Thumb Hero
styles.description: An oversized segmented control gets a close-up: a cursor slides in, presses, and the white thumb snaps to the other segment as icons swap with a spring.

cards.name: shot-transitions
cards.summary: Three handoff recipes for matching scene energy: flash cut, braking whip pan, and portal mask wipe.
cards.use: Any shot-to-shot junction (technique card: select one variant per seam during the storyboard phase after arranging shots).
cards.duration: n/a (technique card; frame allocations for each variant are detailed in the parameter table, deducted from adjacent shot budgets).
cards.energy: n/a (technique card, does not consume an energy slot).
cards.intention: Individual shot cards in the library manage only their own entrance and outro settle; how shots connect with one another has historically lacked explicit vocabulary—naked hard cuts at seams bleed away the cinematic atmosphere painstakingly cultivated shot by shot. Universally acclaimed launch videos (e.g., Linear Releases/Agent, reverse-engineered frame-by-frame on 2026-07-11) feature zero bare cuts: scene changes rely on spatial depth journeys, focus relays, or blackout title-card pauses. This card codifies three foundational recipes: white flash over hard cut, whip-pan using motion blur to mask scene swaps, and portal window zoom entering detailed environments.

styles.label: Flash Cut
styles.description: The camera pushes in and a white flash straddles the cut, hiding the page swap inside the flare.
styles.use: Page-to-page cut with continuous interaction and matching energy

styles.label: Whip Pan
styles.description: The camera whips sideways so hard the middle frames smear illegible, and the new scene is waiting when it stops.
styles.use: Fast-paced feature sequence: light, rapid transition saving frames

styles.label: Mask Wipe
styles.description: A real element in the page — a card — scales up into a full-screen window, and the next scene grows out from inside it.
styles.use: Semantic seam: overview -> detail view ("click this card to enter its world")

cards.name: slam-entrance-moves
cards.summary: Three high-energy arrivals: a perspective snap, a score drop, and an impact burst that pushes nearby elements.
cards.use: Heavyweight entry for hero and KPI cards; impact-feedback handles post-landing response, while this card treats the arrival itself as the impact
cards.duration: Action phase 6–22f + impact aftershocks ~16f + hold >=45f (demo: A 120f / B 135f / C 140f)
cards.energy: High
cards.intention: The ceiling for entrance intensity in the library had been deck-deal-flyin's "dealing cards"—swift, but lacking weight. This card introduces the "slam" tier in three flavors: Variant A delivers directionality—the card whips in grazing the lens with exaggerated fisheye perspective, snapping flat with the stylish flair of anime Kanada-style choreography; Variant B delivers weight—a KPI card drops from 2.6x scale in front of the lens, triggering shock rings, debris particles, screen shake, and white flashes on the exact same frame with the impact of a sports scoreboard; Variant C delivers propagation—building atop B's triad, shockwave fronts sweep across adjacent cards to visibly shove them aside before rebounding, demonstrating raw physical power through "shaking its neighbors." Choose according to narrative needs: use A to announce "it has arrived," B to announce "it is heavy," and C to announce "it shook the entire house."

styles.label: Kanada Perspective Snap
styles.description: Kanada-style snap: perspective 300 to 1500, rotate3d 58 degrees to flat, scale 1.7 to 1 in 18 frames, with a 4-frame overshoot as long shadows settle.
styles.use: Hero card dynamic entrance with anime flair

styles.label: Score Slam
styles.description: A card drops from 2.5x scale and 5 degrees in six accelerating frames; the landing frame fires a shock ring, dust, and screen shake at once.
styles.use: Heavyweight numeric KPI / score entrance

styles.label: Impact Burst Kit
styles.description: The full landing kit plus a physically-timed shockwave that shoves neighboring cards 30px outward with damped tilts as it passes.
styles.use: Full-screen shockwave displacing neighboring elements on populated pages

cards.name: space-camera-moves
cards.summary: Three spatial camera moves: exploded assembly, subject-locked rotation, and a drone-like dive to the landing point.
cards.use: Hero sequences treating a 2D page as a physical 3D object; both variants are "major maneuvers," use <=2 times total per video
cards.duration: A 170f (5.7s, full sequence of explode-hover-recombine-ending title); C 105f (3.5s, dive 69f + settled hold 36f) one-way dive
cards.energy: High
cards.intention: The depth-layer card adds depth to panning—layers move, but the page remains a page. These two recipes go further: the entire page is treated as a 3D physical object, with the camera (or world) executing live-action-grade maneuvers around it. The two variants serve distinct narrative roles: Variant A says "look at what it is made of" (deconstructed exhibition, Apple keynote visual language); Variant C says "slam from global overhead straight into the hero" (god's-eye perspective plunging into a hero close-up, wide -> focal point).

styles.label: Exploded View
styles.description: The page tilts into 3D and its parts blast apart along Z, hover a beat, then reassemble in reverse with a closing shake.
styles.use: Architecture / anatomy showcase: "what is inside the product"; module overview

styles.label: Drone Dive Landing
styles.description: From a near-vertical hover the camera plunges, then air-brakes to a stop on the hero card close-up.
styles.use: Opening establishing shot into subject; chapter launch diving into a point

cards.name: speed-ramp-freeze
cards.summary: A freeze used for on-screen annotation before motion resumes.
cards.use: Pausing to direct viewer attention to a key focal point during card streams or long lateral pans; tutorial explanations and evaluation contexts
cards.energy: Medium-high (velocity contrast itself delivers the energy beat)
cards.intention: Constant linear flow reads like a slide deck (R2); continuous fast motion prevents viewers from absorbing key points (R3). Freeze-annotate halts motion decisively mid-flight—circling the highlight with a marker before resuming. The technical root is frame remapping (slope equals velocity), while the semantic intent is "pausing the class to highlight the board."

styles.label: Freeze Annotate
styles.description: The stream freezes mid-flow, a circled annotation pops on the frozen frame, then everything thaws and keeps moving.

cards.name: spotlight-hero-card
cards.summary: A spotlight selects one card, the camera pushes diagonally, the card lifts for two outline passes, then returns to the page.
cards.use: Single-hero product openings; establishing an atomic unit (card, item, module) as the central protagonist of the video
cards.duration: 172f (~5.7s; lock f34 -> touchdown f142 -> 30f true static hold)
cards.energy: Medium (highest texture and polish, slow and deliberate rhythm)
cards.intention: Telling a focused opening story: this single card is the atomic unit of the product. The spotlight guides viewer attention, elevation provides volume and weight, the contour beam acts as a scanning metaphor, and reseating confirms it belongs to the page layout.

styles.label: Spotlight Hero Card
styles.description: A spotlight selects one card, the camera pushes diagonally, the card lifts for two outline passes, then returns to the page.

cards.name: spotlight-sweep-moves
cards.summary: Three dark-scene spotlight moves: a wake-sleep sweep, an edge-glow pan with purple bleed, and a radial reveal expanding from a corner.
cards.use: Introducing UI panels and feature areas sequentially in dark brand videos; bringing an interface on-screen by "lighting it up" from a black void; lighting transitions between chapters
cards.duration: 3.5–4.5s per variant; A and B can link into a continuous tour sequence
cards.energy: Medium-low (restrained, mysterious; peak impact at the instant of illumination)
cards.intention: In a black void, viewers only see what light reveals—spotlights serve simultaneously as illumination, camera movement, and editing cut: wherever the beam travels, that section debuts; when the beam departs, it takes its bow. All three variants share the signature motif of a "rim-hugging purple glow ray" (a light ray hugging UI borders, logos, and top edges; the glow must be bright and soft, acting as light "caressing" the interface rather than a mechanical stroke animation). The vital rule is **constant velocity**: beam translation and expansion must be strictly linear—easing gives light perceived "intent," whereas constant velocity conveys the mechanical sweep of a searchlight (Variant C precedent: linear velocity with an excessive final radius saturates in the first 1/4, failing to read as constant).

styles.label: Glow Wake Sleep Panel
styles.description: Wake-and-sleep sweep: a reveal mask follows the light head left to right — lit where it passes, sinking back to dark behind it.
styles.use: Dark brand video introducing single UI panel with wake and sleep staging

styles.label: Slide Spotlight Pan
styles.description: Edge-hugging glow: the beam rounds the corner and rides the top edge, violet bleed seeping into the UI, while the panel slides opposite like a camera pan.
styles.use: Horizontal tour across wide board, illuminating functional zones in turn

styles.label: Corner Spotlight Reveal
styles.description: A radial spotlight expands from the corner at strictly linear speed — lit inside, black outside — until the full screen is on. Light as the transition.
styles.use: Dark opening illuminating interface; light transition between segments

cards.name: steep-tilt-glide
cards.summary: A page stands at a steep 60-degree perspective and glides across a fixed camera with speed ghosting while text settles onto the surface mid-flight.
cards.use: Showpiece tour for long pages or multi-section UIs (content gliding across a locked camera position); dark stage neon aesthetic; complementary "lateral glancing" setup to graze-face-tour
cards.duration: 4s (120f) single shot; can extend for wider pages
cards.energy: Medium-high (steep perspective showcase + continuous motion, but steady pacing)
cards.intention: Standing the page upright like an angled wall: the camera remains completely stationary, locked in a steep 60-degree perspective that puts the right edge right in the viewer's face while the left edge recedes into the vanishing point, while the page itself glides sideways across its own plane—content streaming past like subway cars. The core principle is **moving object, locked camera**: perspective, origin, and rotY remain constant throughout; the only variable in motion is the page's local translateX. If the camera moves, it turns into camera acrobatics; here, the focus is "the page presenting itself." The angle converged over three rounds to an exact 60 degrees (-45 deg "wrong" -> -53 deg "steeper" -> -60 deg selected).

styles.label: Steep Tilt Glide
styles.description: A page stands at a steep 60-degree perspective and glides across a fixed camera with speed ghosting while text settles onto the surface mid-flight.

cards.name: stroke-segment-build
cards.summary: Disconnected title strokes illuminate in a scrambled order and become readable only when the final segments snap into place.
cards.use: Suspenseful reveals for product names or major milestones at video openings; <=1 time per film; division of labor with type-assembly / draw-svg-trace: those cards showcase "watching letters being built or drawn," while this card focuses on "delayed revelation of meaning"
cards.duration: 165f (5.5s; reveal at f105 followed by 2s hold)
cards.energy: Low start building to medium finish (suspenseful; landing frame serves as energy climax)
cards.intention: The Alien opening title precedent: titles are not drawn, they "materialize"—deconstructed into discrete stroke segments lighting up out of sequence, keeping viewers guessing through 70% of the duration before the final key strokes click into place, suddenly revealing the word. The "moment of recognition" is the hook, and its power depends on how long illegibility is maintained and how late key strokes are delayed.

styles.label: Stroke Segment Build
styles.description: Disconnected title strokes illuminate in a scrambled order and become readable only when the final segments snap into place.

cards.name: tear-streak-transitions
cards.summary: A high-energy tear: horizontal glitch strips whose displacement hides the hard cut.
cards.use: High-energy page transitions: digital glitch / disruption semantics; strip-level tearing that keeps page integrity intact while pushing energy to the max.
cards.energy: High
cards.intention: This card governs **strip-level digital tearing**—the page is sliced into horizontal bands moving at high velocity, yet the content within each band remains intact. This represents a taste boundary defined by repeated review rulings: fragmented block transitions were struck down three times in succession (doom-melt vertical drip, pixel-dissolve black tile flips, and facade-block 3D tumbling bricks were all eliminated), whereas strip-based transitions passed. Fragmented blocks read as "the page is being destroyed," whereas horizontal strips read as "the page is undergoing high-velocity motion"—maintaining structural integrity while driving kinetic energy to its peak. Horizontal tear: strips jitter with left/right displacement + dual-color silhouette ghosting (a restrained take on RGB split: two monochromatic silhouette duplicates of the page content rendered strictly in the scene's two accent colors, offset by ±12px). Ideal for system disruption or instantaneous state-flip semantics—the demo applies it to a state transition where a deployment console snaps from "Rolling out 99%" to "is live."

styles.label: Glitch Displace
styles.description: A high-energy tear: horizontal glitch strips whose displacement hides the hard cut.
styles.use: Glitch / disruption semantics; forceful page swap before climax

cards.name: tension-camera-moves
cards.summary: Two emotional camera tools: a frozen orbit and an isolating pull-back.
cards.use: Camera language for emotional beats (awe / consolidation); complements the showy acrobatics of space-camera-moves—these two moves are minimal in physical displacement but heavy in emotional gravity
cards.duration: 5–6s per variant (150–170f); <=2 variants total per video (<=1 time each)
cards.energy: A High / B Low resolution
cards.intention: The space-camera-moves recipes are high-energy showcases that treat a page as a 3D physical object; these two variants take the opposite approach—physically restrained motion where all dynamic force is invested in emotional semantics: Variant A says "this moment is worth stopping time to inspect" (elements frozen in mid-motion while the camera orbits to observe); Variant B says "in the end, only this one thing remains" (surroundings extinguish layer by layer as the camera pulls back, isolating a solitary element to resolve the entire piece). Each variant occupies a distinct emotional niche, serving as direct vocabulary for the question: "what should the audience feel in this beat?"

styles.label: Bullet Time Freeze Orbit
styles.description: A growing chart freezes mid-animation while the camera orbits the hovering UI plane 55 degrees and back, then time resumes.
styles.use: Coronation moment for core data / chart; "worth stopping the clock to see"

styles.label: Pull Back Isolation
styles.description: The camera pulls back from one glowing card while its siblings go dark by distance, leaving it alone in a black field.
styles.use: Outro convergence: "the whole video was for this single number" finale

cards.name: terminal-3d
cards.summary: Three terminal windows float at different poses in 3D space; the camera flies between them with a sine pull-back, and at each stop a command types out and its results slide in line by line.
cards.use: CLI / workflow demos for developer products: turning a "3-step command" into a 3-stop spatial journey
cards.duration: ~8.2s (246f@30fps; ~2–3s hold at each of the 3 stops + two 30f flight segments)
cards.energy: Medium (flight provides motion, typing provides cadence, overall steady technical narrative; concluding on a luminous READY beacon)
cards.intention: Terminal output is inherently anti-cinematic flat scrolling; this card translates it into spatial storytelling: each command occupies a physical window in 3D space, with the camera visiting each window like walking through a server room. Mid-flight pull-backs give the audience glimpses of surrounding windows—imparting a holistic sense of workflow structure.

styles.label: Terminal 3D
styles.description: Three terminal windows float at different poses in 3D space; the camera flies between them with a sine pull-back, and at each stop a command types out and its results slide in line by line.

cards.name: text-as-mask
cards.summary: Product footage moves inside oversized title letters before the type expands until the footage takes over the frame.
cards.use: Opening or chapter cards merging brand tagline and product footage; typography acts as the doorway, product lives inside
cards.duration: 165f (entrance 18f + intra-glyph drift 78f + inhale 8f + plunge takeover 24f + settle/hold 37f)
cards.energy: Medium-High (composed drift, explosive single burst during takeover)
cards.intention: Typography and product footage competing for screen space is an age-old challenge—displaying typography before footage is slow, while overlaying typography on footage feels cluttered. This technique unifies both: glyphs act as masks, revealing product footage exclusively through strokes, allowing viewers to absorb copy and product texture simultaneously; at the conclusion, glyphs expand past frame boundaries, letting footage naturally take over the full screen—telling the story of "stepping through the brand into the product" in a single continuous shot while doubling as a chapter transition. (Shares lineage with transition-travel Style A counter-tunnel: there the camera dives into letter counters, whereas here letterforms expand outward—former moves camera, latter moves doorway).

styles.label: Text As Mask
styles.description: Product footage moves inside oversized title letters before the type expands until the footage takes over the frame.

cards.name: text-column-converge
cards.summary: Two words pinned at opposite screen edges hard-swap through options, then slide together exactly once to lock into the final phrase.
cards.use: Sections where feature lists converge into product name / slogan ("NEW × sequence of features → NEW <product name>"); keynote-style recaps, version number reveals
cards.duration: Cycling 7–16f/word × 8–9 words + convergence ~36f + static hold after subtitle; full sequence ~5–6s
cards.energy: Medium-low (machine rhythm, small-type specification list aesthetic, not aggressive slamming type)
cards.intention: Two words pinned at opposite screen edges confront each other like directory index headers, leading viewers to assume they are just cycling subtitles; only when the final word settles do they realize the left and right halves belong to the same sentence — a single continuous convergence reveals the entire cycle in retrospect as dramatic suspense. The critical requirement is to **pin positions dead**: during the cycling phase, word coordinates do not budge by a single pixel, and left/right screen margins are strictly identical (reference measured at 412 vs 413 @1280); any progressive contraction prematurely spoils the convergence, diluting a reveal into a progress bar. Convergence is permitted to happen exactly once, and must occur strictly after the final word settles — this is a concluding reveal, not continuous animation.

styles.label: Text Column Converge
styles.description: Two words pinned at opposite screen edges hard-swap through options, then slide together exactly once to lock into the final phrase.

cards.name: theme-switch-moves
cards.summary: Two theme-change patterns: a diagonal sweep that recolors content in place, and a command-palette ripple with a clear cause and effect.
cards.use: Narrative segments for dark mode / theme switching; identical UI "changing colors before your eyes" rather than cutting to a new scene
cards.energy: A Medium / B Medium-High (combo variant features complete causal chain)
cards.intention: Two filming methods for dark/light mode switching. A (standard in Notion/Figma/Linear): a 15-degree diagonal boundary with bright light sweeps across the screen (in demo, sweeping from switch on right toward left); as boundary passes, light elements switch to dark **in place**, with dual themes briefly coexisting across identical layout—viewers witness "the same UI reskinning," not a transition. B (combo variant): Cmd+K palette receives "dark" and Enter is pressed; palette collapses into a bright dot, and dark ripples **radiate from that dot** across full UI—establishing a fully legible causal chain of "command triggers reskin." Critical combo requirement: ripple origin must match palette collapse point, and trigger frame must be collapse completion frame.

styles.label: Theme Sweep Toggle
styles.description: The dark theme sweeps across as a slanted clip-path edge with a glowing 4px line, recoloring everything it passes in one 38-frame pass.
styles.use: Direct theme switching showcase

styles.label: Palette Theme Ripple
styles.description: The command palette collapses to a bright point, and from that point a circular ripple floods the new theme across the screen.
styles.use: Command palette + theme synchronization highlight

cards.name: timeline-travel
cards.summary: The camera accelerates along a horizontal version timeline, raises cards at each stop, then brakes sharply on the final milestone.
cards.use: Changelog, milestone, or product evolution sections (another way to shoot "we ship continuously"); complements scroll-brake-moves: that card is a vertical list brake, this card is a horizontal time journey
cards.energy: Medium-high (acceleration to sudden brake rhythm profile)
cards.intention: Shooting a product's release history as an expedition along a chronological axis (reference: The Kingdom opening title sequence): the camera executes a three-stage variable speed pan (gentle launch -> sprint -> abrupt brake) as v1.0 / v2.0 / v3.0 markers flash by, each raising a card via spring pop off the baseline—history rushes past outside the window, braking sharply on "today" with a punch-in. Speed itself communicates rapid development; the abrupt halt signals "now is what matters most."

styles.label: Timeline Travel
styles.description: The camera accelerates along a horizontal version timeline, raises cards at each stop, then brakes sharply on the final milestone.

cards.name: title-demote-to-label
cards.summary: A centered headline stands for a beat, then shrinks and slides to the top-left corner to become a section label as content grows beneath it.
cards.use: Chapter openers (headline claims the spotlight first, then yields to content); section transitions in tutorials / feature demos; Variant B adds product cues for text/editor tools
cards.duration: A ~3.7s (112f) / B ~4.5s (134f); demo chains both variants in 246f
cards.energy: Low-medium (editorial layout transformation, atmospheric shot)
cards.intention: The conventional fate of chapter headings is "enter → vanish → content appears," leaving heading and content disconnected. This card lets the heading **demote rather than exit**: large centered type holds for a beat to declare the topic, then in a single continuous tween scales to 0.3x and glides to the top-left corner, landing as the section label — remaining on screen, but transitioning from protagonist to signpost. Viewers receive effortless spatial continuity: the massive word they just saw is now the label in the upper-left corner, signaling what the section discusses. The content skeleton begins growing while demotion is underway, achieving a zero-dead-air handoff.

styles.label: Title Demote To Label
styles.description: A centered headline stands for a beat, then shrinks and slides to the top-left corner to become a section label as content grows beneath it.

cards.name: trailer-grammar-moves
cards.summary: A trailer bumper hook: three 9-frame rapid cuts, a beat of black silence, then the opening title card.
cards.use: Opening hook for trailers (cold open): packing three attention-grabbing shots before the main film, followed by a silent beat before the formal title
cards.energy: A High
cards.intention: Rhythm cards in the library manage distinct segments: beat-cut governs cut placement, and rhythm-interrupt governs interruptions. This card governs **structural trailer moments**—not how an individual shot moves, but how major joints of the entire film connect: Variant A serves as the opening hook—stuffing three hyper-engaging shots into 0.9 seconds before the main feature, followed by a silent beat of black void before opening the title—a "trailer for the trailer."

styles.label: Trailer Bumper
styles.description: Three 9-frame shots hard-cut in strict time, each with a tiny internal push, then 6 frames of black silence before the title rises.
styles.use: Cold open hook before main video

cards.name: transition-hidden-cut
cards.summary: Three ways to conceal the edit: foreground occlusion, opposing impacts, and a brief amber light leak at the cut.
cards.use: Shot junctions requiring "seamless scene swaps" or "ceremonial impact reveals" (technique card: evaluated at the same layer as the three shot-transitions variants).
cards.duration: n/a (technique card; frame allocations for each variant are detailed in the parameter table, deducted from adjacent shot budgets).
cards.energy: n/a (technique card, does not consume an energy slot).
cards.intention: Belonging to the same lineage as shot-transitions Variant A (flash-cut): while flash-cut masks a hard cut beneath a burst of white light, these three variants employ three distinct "distractions"—a foreground card sweeping past the lens (A), the collision frame of an opposing impact (B), or an amber light leak climbing to its peak (C). The shared governing principle is magician's misdirection: executing the hard cut during the 1–3 frames when the viewer's gaze is captured by massive motion or blinding light; by the time attention returns, the scene has already changed, leaving the audience "unable to spot the scissors." Flash-cut is the most utilitarian option; choose A for directional momentum, B for ceremonial impact, and C for warmth and organic texture.

styles.label: Invisible Cut
styles.description: An oversized card sweeps past the lens with heavy motion blur, and the background swaps scenes inside the fully-covered frames.
styles.use: Seamless page-to-page transition for pseudo one-take flow

styles.label: Versus Slam
styles.description: Two half-screens with slanted edges charge from opposite sides and collide; the impact frame is the cut — white flash, shake, VS stamp.
styles.use: Comparison opening / chapter header: new vs old, dual products, before/after

styles.label: Light Leak Burn
styles.description: Three amber light blooms sweep the diagonal, and at peak coverage the old page hard-cuts away beneath the flare.
styles.use: Warm filmic chapter transition: softer, warmer, and more directional than white flash

cards.name: transition-travel
cards.summary: A passage transition that pushes through the counter of a giant letterform into the next scene.
cards.use: Seams between two shots sharing an "element/container" spatial relationship (technique card: selected complementarily with the three shot-transitions variants).
cards.duration: n/a (technique card; demo 150f, main push action segment 52f, preceding/trailing holds budgeted separately, frames deducted from adjacent shot budgets).
cards.energy: n/a (technique card, does not consume an energy slot).
cards.intention: The three shot-transitions recipes are "handoff" types—the outgoing shot wraps up, the incoming shot enters, and the seam relies on a white flash, motion blur, or an opening window to disguise the cut. This card is a **"travel"** type—the incoming background pre-exists as a genuine physical element within the foreground frame (a hole in a letterform), and the camera dives through via a single continuous spatial trajectory. The viewer follows the same physical entity from start to finish, with no handoff beat. Selection criteria: if the incoming scene can "pre-exist" inside the foreground → travel; if the two scenes simply share sequential order without spatial nesting → handoff. The semantic concept of letterform travel is **"the title is the doorway"** (unifying the chapter title card and the transition into a single action).

styles.label: Letterform Zoom
styles.description: The next page shows through a giant letterform cut as a mask; the camera zooms through the letter until it swallows the frame.
styles.use: Chapter title -> body text: high-energy alternative to black card titles

cards.name: type-and-filter
cards.summary: A real interface types a search, collapses the grid to one result, then clicks through into the detail view.
cards.use: "Operational narrative" segments in feature demos; any interactive flow involving search, filtering, and drilling into details
cards.energy: Medium (a composed beat following high-energy card-dealing sequences)
cards.intention: Guiding the viewer to "follow along step-by-step": clearly see what was typed, how the page responded, and where the cursor clicked. This is the only shot in the entire video simulating realistic human operation; rhythm must feel like a human hand, not a script.

styles.label: Type And Filter
styles.description: A real interface types a search, collapses the grid to one result, then clicks through into the detail view.

cards.name: type-assembly-moves
cards.summary: Three typography assemblies: split-letter rise, drifting convergence, and text flowing along a path.
cards.use: Entrances for large titles / slogans; belongs to the broader title-entrance family alongside type-entrance-moves and document-typewriter-reveal; ≤2 types across full video
cards.duration: 4–5.5s per variant (action segments: A ~56f / B ~104f / C ~110f; full demo duration including hold: A 130f / B 150f / C 160f, exporting respective `*_DURATION`)
cards.energy: A Medium / B Medium-high / C Medium
cards.intention: Title entrances already offer in-place transformation styles (character drop / typewriter — text morphs within its original footprint). This card introduces the "assembly" family: characters **converge from elsewhere** to form the title, where the motion trajectory itself tells a story. Variant A (Piano Keys) — letters slide upward from behind an invisible baseline clip, crisp and rational, offering the highest versatility; Variant B (Title Sequence) — characters drift in from scattered directions with defocus and lock in with deep ink pulses, evoking Stranger Things title sequence ceremonial weight, ideal for brand unveils; Variant C (Semantic Path) — characters flow along an ascending curve in single file before standing upright, where the path can trace a financial growth chart, uniting typography and data into a single narrative.

styles.label: Split Text Stagger
styles.description: Each character rises inside its own overflow box from 115% with a 10% overshoot, two frames apart, as the baseline grows beneath.
styles.use: Universal default: crisp and rational

styles.label: Drift Assembly
styles.description: Characters drift in from seeded directions with blur, locking into place one by one, each lock landing a darkening pulse.
styles.use: Brand name / intro title reveal

styles.label: Text On Path
styles.description: Characters slide in single-file along a bezier curve, rotating with the tangent, then straighten level over 12 frames.
styles.use: Text following meaningful path (growth curve / flowchart)

cards.name: type-entrance-moves
cards.summary: Letters falling under gravity and bouncing into alignment as a title entrance.
cards.use: Entrances for large titles / chapter title cards; mutually exclusive with type-assembly-moves (assembly style) and document-typewriter-reveal (typewriter style) within the same category
cards.duration: 5s per variant (including hold and static rest; motion segment ~116f, demo 150f)
cards.energy: Medium-high (physical playfulness)
cards.intention: The title entrance library already includes typewriter style (sober, document feel) and assembly style (words converging from elsewhere); this card introduces physical comedy — characters plummeting from the sky, bouncing off the floor, settling at precarious angles, and snapping into perfect alignment on the final beat, ideal for lighthearted openers (demo drops the brand name "Shotcraft", with subtitle "Every shot lands on the beat." emerging on the snap beat). Title entrances across the same film must be ≤2 types (P4).

styles.label: Letter Drop Physics
styles.description: Characters fall from above under gravity, bounce twice, land crooked, then square up together on the final beat.
styles.use: Playful title ice-breaker with kinetic vitality

cards.name: type-rhythm-sync
cards.summary: Two voice-and-beat synchronizations: font weight pulsing on percussion and spoken words filling like karaoke.
cards.use: Sections where headlines / slogans bind tightly to audio tracks; Variant A binds to musical tempo (drum hits), Variant B binds to voiceover (spoken word tracking)
cards.duration: A FontWeightPump 165f / B KaraokeFillSync 150f; A 128 BPM 14f per beat with 9–13f decay window; B 18–33f per word based on speech cadence
cards.energy: A High (dance-floor pulse) / B Medium (guided reading flow)
cards.intention: Previous typography cards in the library focused entirely on "how text enters the frame," offering nothing for "how text already on screen lives and breathes with the audio." These two variants provide the answer: Variant A turns headlines into rhythmic organs — letter strokes swell into heavy weights on bass hits and snap back, dancing to the beat as a visual subwoofer for high-energy segments; Variant B turns slogans into guided subtitles — words fill with color from left to right as the voiceover speaks them, pulling the viewer's gaze along during spoken emphasis segments. Their common principle: **text remains stationary while properties animate** — zero displacement, zero entrance/exit, purely font-weight and color breathing in lockstep with the sound track.

styles.label: Font Weight Pump
styles.description: On each hit the strokes jump bold and spring back thin over 10 frames; accent beats also widen the word 8%.
styles.use: Music-driven high-energy beat; typography acts as bass kick

styles.label: Karaoke Fill Sync
styles.description: Each word fills dark-to-bright left to right at speech speed and stays lit, a reading underline tracking the active word.
styles.use: Voiceover emphasis; guided eye flow across multi-word slogan

cards.name: typewriter-moves
cards.summary: A three-act typing narrative: a plain word, a hesitation and deletion, then a faster retype of the selling point.
cards.use: Slogan/value-prop title cards, negative framing copy; text entrance with built-in temporality
cards.energy: Medium-low
cards.intention: Typing is the only text entrance with built-in temporality — characters arriving one by one is rhythm itself, requiring no auxiliary motion effects. Variant A treats typing as a **monologue**: typing out a mediocre word (in demo: "just a slideshow" beneath the eyebrow Introducing video-shotcraft) → pausing in hesitation → backspacing to delete → retyping the true selling point ("your cinematic crew") with greater speed. This hesitation-negation-declaration three-act drama draws all its emotional punch from the speed differentials between the three gears.

styles.label: Error Retype
styles.description: Type, pause with a blinking cursor, backspace, retype without hesitation — a three-act correction that reads as human.
styles.use: Slogan hesitation and correction play; negation copywriting

cards.name: ui-strip-away-outro
cards.summary: After Publish is clicked the editor UI evaporates layer by layer from the edges inward, leaving one button to slide center, grow, and hand off to the wordmark.
cards.use: Outros with "publish / complete" semantics; product finales conveying "one click and all complexity vanishes"
