cards.duration: ~4.8s (144f: cursor in place 34f -> evaporation ~40f -> button solo -> wordmark handoff -> wordmark hold >=1s)
cards.energy: Medium (quiet operation upfront, continuous exit mid-shot, no sudden impact)
cards.intention: Standard shot library finales are additive: outro-group-photo-launch flies in elements for a group photo; logo stings freeze before playing an easter egg. This card provides the sole "subtractive" path—a single click detonates the entire UI's departure, leaving only the semantic focal point (the clicked button) in a black void, translating "publishing = complexity vanishes to zero" into motion narrative. Two critical rules: **evaporation must be orderly**—progressing from periphery to center every 4f per layer, each carrying directional displacement (dispersing outward offscreen); chaotic order or simultaneous extinction looks like a power outage; **the button is the sole survivor and must migrate**—during evaporation, it glides from the toolbar corner to the screen center, enlarging by 1.5x while white glow intensifies against the darkening stage, completing its elevation from "UI control" to "ceremonial protagonist," before finally fading out to hand the dark stage over to the wordmark.

styles.label: Ui Strip Away Outro
styles.description: After Publish is clicked the editor UI evaporates layer by layer from the edges inward, leaving one button to slide center, grow, and hand off to the wordmark.

cards.name: ui-to-brand-morph
cards.summary: Two UI-to-brand morphs: an icon flips flat and blooms into a logo mark, and an input field contracts into a capsule as glyphs assemble the logo.
cards.use: Brand finale / penultimate outro shot; visual argument that "the UI you use every day is this very brand"
cards.energy: Medium-high (finishing touch, told through a single complete transformation)
cards.intention: The brand outro library previously provided two main avenues: brand-ink-open is an opening draw-and-stamp, while outro-group-photo-launch gathers elements for an ensemble photo (assembling without morphing). This card adds a third: **product UI elements themselves morph into brand symbols**—Variant A flips an icon flat to become the logo mark (in-place entity exchange); Variant B gathers the input field that appeared repeatedly throughout the film into the brand logo after its final send action (multi-element drop-in assembly). The audience sees not just "a logo appeared," but realizes "the tool we just used is the brand itself"—the causal chain itself serves as the brand argument.

styles.label: Icon Flip Bloom
styles.description: The icon rocks twice, flips flat to a sliver with double ghosting, swaps identity at the thinnest frame, and unfolds into the video-shotcraft Frame Chisel mark — the amber cut slicing in on a second beat — as the wordmark lands.
styles.use: Single icon product: magical flip-and-morph when icon and logo forms differ

styles.label: Input Morph Assemble
styles.description: Send is clicked, the text flies off, the input box spring-morphs into a capsule that becomes the frame stem of the mark; the top and bottom bars and the amber cut drop into dashed construction outlines to assemble the video-shotcraft mark.
styles.use: Rectangular UI (input / card) as protagonist; logo decomposed into geometric elements

cards.name: value-stagger-gradient
cards.summary: Sixteen bars rise in a staggered sweep where height, hue, travel distance and blur are each spread as a gradient across the row, then a second beat re-origins the stagger at the center so the pulse amplitude fans out symmetrically.
cards.use: Demonstrating craft and parametric motion capabilities; directly applicable as entrances for data grids, audio visualizers, or equalizer interfaces.
cards.energy: Medium-High (Beat one is a continuous rollout; beat two's center pulse is an explicit sharp peak)
cards.intention: Stagger is typically used merely to offset time. This card demonstrates that stagger can also offset **values**—a single index dictates both "when it moves" and "how much it moves." The two beats form a controlled experiment: beat one originates at the first index (gradient unfolds monotonically left-to-right), while beat two relocates origin to the center (gradient unfolds symmetrically across the central axis). Viewers perceive not two disparate animations, but a single recipe with an adjusted parameter. Code captions on screen update synchronously to reflect the corresponding stagger invocation, rendering the concept explicit.

styles.label: Value Stagger Gradient
styles.description: Sixteen bars rise in a staggered sweep where height, hue, travel distance and blur are each spread as a gradient across the row, then a second beat re-origins the stagger at the center so the pulse amplitude fans out symmetrically.

cards.name: vertical-word-roll-blur-cycle
cards.summary: The closing word of a tagline rolls vertically through a three-line reel, neighbouring rows blurring into grey depth while the settled word takes the accent color.
cards.use: "Crafted for ___" / "Built for ___" sentence stems + audience/target enumeration value props; crisp, clean beat in light-background brand videos
cards.duration: ~5.0s (150f@30fps: static hold → 3 word cycles → full group fade-out at tail)
cards.energy: Medium (steady 3-beat cadence, no peak)
cards.intention: Swapping the concluding word of a sentence works best via a vertical reel rather than crossfading: a reel carries inherent **directionality** (flipping upward like pages), signaling to the audience that "more is coming." This card's two identity signatures are the **vertical blur** on neighboring rows (simulating cylindrical depth of field and mechanical defocus) and the **landing tint** (grey → accent color, declaring "this is the answer"). The sentence stem (demo: `Crafted for`) remains completely motionless throughout — the viewer's eyes stay fixed on the reel; any movement in the stem dissolves the sense of enumeration.

styles.label: Vertical Word Roll Blur Cycle
styles.description: The closing word of a tagline rolls vertically through a three-line reel, neighbouring rows blurring into grey depth while the settled word takes the accent color.

cards.name: voice-waveform-live
cards.summary: A recording capsule shows 64 live bars that surge with speech, shrink to a dotted line in pauses, and collapse on submit.
cards.use: Feature shots for voice input / AI assistants signaling "listening to you"; segments lacking UI content to showcase but requiring continuous vitality to sustain the screen
cards.duration: 172f (~5.7s: entrance 14f + speech 1.4s + pause 0.8s + speech 1.4s + submit collapse / tuck into bubble 0.8s + hold 0.7s)
cards.energy: Medium (functional vitality, not visual flexing)
cards.intention: This card provides a **functional** waveform: a live receipt of "listening to you." The linchpin lies in causality: the waveform pulses with "user speech" as a core product capability, rather than decorative packaging dancing to BGM. Waveform surges when speaking, collapses into dotted lines during pauses, and historical waves stream leftward—viewers perceive "it is truly listening" from the wave undulations, sustaining 6s+ of screen time purely through vitality without needing other content. Division of labor with gauge-readout-moves: gauges represent mechanical rituals of "reporting a value," whereas this card represents the vital signs of "continuous monitoring," devoid of terminal values.

styles.label: Voice Waveform Live
styles.description: A recording capsule shows 64 live bars that surge with speech, shrink to a dotted line in pauses, and collapse on submit.

cards.name: wall-reveal-moves
cards.summary: Two in-place wall reveals: sequential bento lights and a wireframe drawing itself into a finished interface.
cards.use: Monolithic reveals of feature walls, card grids, and full-page dashboards; sections where content is already in place and should "materialize" rather than "fly in."
cards.duration: ~5s per variant (A 150f / B 150f @ 30fps, including establishing hold and static finish)
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intention: When asking "how does a wall of content enter," the library previously had only one answer: deck-deal-flyin—high energy, displacement-driven, "items streaming in." But not every wall should stream in: brand segments require dignity, and "from concept to production" requires process. The shared principle of these two variants is **non-displacement batch entrance**—elements materialize in place, layout holds true from frame one, and viewers observe a wavefront of state change sweeping across a wall rather than flying objects. When selecting, ask: should this wall "flood in" or "illuminate in place"? The former points to deck-deal-flyin; the latter belongs here.

styles.label: Bento Light Up
styles.description: A dark 3x2 bento wall waits dimmed; amber light traces each cell border and the content brightens and lifts, cell by cell, until a slow push seals it.
styles.use: Solemn / dark brand segment: steady, rhythmic feature overview

styles.label: Wireframe Draw On
styles.description: The interface draws itself as blueprint linework first, then a glowing amber scanline sweeps left to right, solidifying wireframe into real UI.
styles.use: "From concept to product" narrative; first complete product reveal

cards.name: white-flash-logo-simplify-cut
cards.summary: A liquid six-color gradient wordmark shimmers in place, the frame flash-burns to white with a blur-and-brightness pulse, and a flat gradient wordmark fades in and settles on the white.
cards.use: Brand sequence resolution (flamboyant demonstration → pristine lockup); transition beat shifting emotion from technical virtuosity to authoritative declaration.
cards.duration: Approx. 4s (120f@30fps; showcase 0–34f · anticipation 34–46f · whiteout surge 44–54f · exposure recovery 54–76f · lockup 72–96f · hold through 120f).
cards.energy: Medium-high (a single pulsed accent, flanked by serene static stages).
cards.intention: First deliver unabashed luxury (an iridescent liquid-metal wash rippling across the letterforms, swept by an angled specular glint), then deploy a white flash to "purify" the mark into a flat, monochromatic logo—communicating to the audience that "the spectacle has concluded; this is its true, authoritative identity." Dimensional reduction serves as visual rhetoric: shifting from emotional texture to rational brand recognition. Both versions share identical font size and layout coordinates, registering as "the same wordmark being purified," rather than an arbitrary image swap.

styles.label: White Flash Logo Simplify Cut
styles.description: A liquid six-color gradient wordmark shimmers in place, the frame flash-burns to white with a blur-and-brightness pulse, and a flat gradient wordmark fades in and settles on the white.

cards.name: wipe-transitions
cards.summary: A geometric wipe: twelve staggered vertical blinds flipping in a wave.
cards.use: Universal transitions where both outgoing and incoming pages remain stationary while a geometric boundary sweeps across to execute the handoff; independent of composition elements, usable anywhere.
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intention: The transition library already features three distinct families: travel moves (diving through), hidden cuts (occluding the cut), and physical slabs (the page as a solid entity). This card introduces the fourth family: **geometric wipes**—both outgoing and incoming pages remain stationary while a geometric boundary sweeps across the frame to execute the handoff. The geometry of the wipe defines its semantic character: vertical strip sweeps embody "venetian blinds flipping vane by vane to turn the page." Contrast with shot-transitions Variant C (portal mask wipe): Variant C relies on real in-page UI elements as masks (dependent on composition), whereas this card is purely geometric—its positioning lies in its universal versatility. Perfectly suited for lateral momentum and page-turning semantics.

styles.label: Blinds Slice
styles.description: Twelve vertical slats flip in a staggered wave — the old page collapsing at one edge as the new one expands from the other, a bright seam riding the wave.
styles.use: Page-turn / progression semantics; horizontal reading flow

cards.name: word-relay-filmstrip
cards.summary: A filmstrip of page cards steps vertically while a serif word relay swaps only its verb, each swap aligned to the center of the current card.
cards.use: "Single subject × multiple capabilities" enumeration sections (Shotcraft frames / builds / ships…); portfolio / case-study flows; multi-scenario product walkthroughs
cards.energy: Medium-low (editorial temperament, rhythm driven by tactile "click" of word swaps)
cards.intention: On the left sits the evidence (page screenshot filmstrip), on the right sits the thesis (large display typography): each time the verb swaps, the filmstrip steps down by one frame to present fresh evidence — copy and visuals annotate each other. The core requirement is **stepped motion**: the left column remains completely static normally, advancing exactly one card height solely at the instant of a word swap (stepping = the physical action of changing evidence); continuous scrolling degrades the left column into decorative background noise, robbing word swaps of their tactile "click." The second requirement is **alignment**: the vertical midpoint of the large text block must align with pixel-level precision to the midpoint of the active page card; any vertical deviation collapses the disciplined elegance of the editorial layout.

cards.use: Three-part value proposition statements (Faster / Tighter / Stronger); brand values segments; mid-section momentum requiring "a distinct world for each word"
cards.energy: Medium-high (3-beat progression + continuous geometric motion + background particles, zero static frames)
cards.intention: A three-part value proposition easily devolves into three hard-cut title cards. The relay approach pairs each word with **a bespoke geometric motif tailored to its meaning**: a spinning dashed circle represents rotary speed ("Faster"), three interlocking circles trimming and contracting represent precision grip ("Tighter"), and a metallic sheen sweep represents hardened substance ("Stronger") — the geometry itself argues on behalf of each adjective. The third word receives elevated hero treatment (chrome sheen sweep + snapping to solid white) because it delivers the conclusion. Floating ambient dust, unified stage lighting, and a bottom 3-segment progress bar stitch the three beats into a single continuous space, avoiding the disjointed feel of three isolated slides.
